assessedActivities.name: Patient fasts
assessedActivities.reason: Patient fasts describes bodily behavior rather than software interaction, so RPA cannot perform it. Fasting does not require creativity or complex interpretation (criterion 5).

assessedActivities.name: Give medicaments
assessedActivities.reason: Give medicaments is physical medication administration by a nurse, not an activity performed through application interfaces. The model supplies no administration rules or other evidence supporting the feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Perform colonoskopy
assessedActivities.reason: Perform colonoskopy is a physical clinical procedure and cannot be executed by an RPA software robot. No supporting evidence establishes any of the nine criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Check electrolytes
assessedActivities.reason: Check electrolytes is a clinical check with no specified software, digital inputs, or unambiguous checking rules. The model does not establish that the activity can be performed through application interfaces without clinical interpretation.

assessedActivities.name: Enter patient into surgery board
assessedActivities.reason: Enter patient into surgery board describes routine recording using a preliminary surgery date, supporting criteria 5 and 7. However, the model does not establish whether the surgery board is digital, so UI-based RPA feasibility cannot be determined.

assessedActivities.reason: Collect and evaluate all results includes clinical evaluation by the ward doctor without specified evaluation rules or software support. Its deadline does not establish rule-based execution or digital availability of the results.

assessedActivities.name: Start of order
assessedActivities.reason: Start of order does not specify software use, digital inputs, or rules for initiating an order. Its machine-operator context is insufficient to establish RPA feasibility or any criterion.

assessedActivities.name: Start of batch
assessedActivities.reason: Start of batch precedes Setup, but the model does not indicate whether it involves physical operations or application interaction. No feasibility criterion is sufficiently supported to establish RPA suitability.

assessedActivities.name: Setup
assessedActivities.reason: Setup occurs in a machine-operation process, without details distinguishing physical setup from software configuration. The model supplies no rules, application interactions, or data evidence supporting RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Release / validation
assessedActivities.reason: Release / validation specifies neither validation rules nor the information and systems used. Its position before production and logistics does not establish rule-based, digital execution or other feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Production
assessedActivities.reason: Production in the Customer Machine Operator pool, followed by Cleaning, indicates a physical production activity rather than an application-interface task. No RPA feasibility criteria are established.

assessedActivities.name: Logistics / warehouse
assessedActivities.reason: Logistics / warehouse runs alongside Production, but the model does not distinguish physical handling from digital administrative work. Without specified software interactions, rules, or data, RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Cleaning
assessedActivities.reason: Cleaning follows production and warehouse operations in the machine-operator pool, indicating physical cleaning rather than digital processing. Such work cannot be performed by RPA through application user interfaces, and no feasibility criteria are established.

assessedActivities.name: End of production
assessedActivities.reason: End of production does not specify whether completion requires physical operations or a software update. No rules, digital data, or application interactions are provided to support feasibility criteria or an RPA decision.

assessedActivities.name: End of batch
assessedActivities.reason: End of batch identifies a completion stage without describing its execution or data requirements. The model does not establish software-based work or any other feasibility criterion, so RPA suitability remains unsupported.

assessedActivities.name: Complete acceptance appointment

assessedActivities.name: Sign acceptance report

assessedActivities.name: Pay invoice
assessedActivities.reason: Payment follows invoice checking, but the payment method, authorization rules, and supporting application are unspecified. This sequence alone does not establish any feasibility criterion or demonstrate that RPA can execute payment.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<bpmn:definitions xmlns:bpmn="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/MODEL" xmlns:bpmndi="http://www.omg.org/spec/BPMN/20100524/DI" xmlns:dc="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DC" xmlns:di="http://www.omg.org/spec/DD/20100524/DI" id="Definitions_1" targetNamespace="http://bpmn.io/schema/bpmn">
  <bpmn:collaboration id="Collaboration_1slfacu">
    <bpmn:participant id="Participant_1qztjjo" processRef="Process_1" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0ykio4b">
      <bpmn:text>Time tracking management data should be recorded for a new employee</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0619tdw" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Event_199cfk1" targetRef="TextAnnotation_0ykio4b" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_06rc5y6">
      <bpmn:text>The “chip card” is the unique time tracking ID in ZEB. Assignment is also required even if no physical chip cards are used, for example when time tracking data is imported or when the QIS terminal is used.</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_08xqino" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_1p09aug" targetRef="TextAnnotation_06rc5y6" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_1na1mc1">
      <bpmn:text>Chip cards (pgd_ze_chip)</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_1chaa1g" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_1p09aug" targetRef="TextAnnotation_1na1mc1" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_1a756w9">
      <bpmn:text>ZEB settings (person_taa_config)</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_1sq9eqa" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_0klxy94" targetRef="TextAnnotation_1a756w9" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_1fcwq7p">
      <bpmn:text>Working time (PAZ)</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0l5z4ju" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_192hz16" targetRef="TextAnnotation_1fcwq7p" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_11k1bz0">
      <bpmn:text>QIS user role assignment (r_kollektionnutzer)</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0pui5wv">
      <bpmn:text>Time recorder, web time recorder and/or employee</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_1xdnwrs">
      <bpmn:text>Based on the working time data, ZEB determines the target working hours. In the case of multiple parallel employment relationships, a person’s target working time is the sum of the target working hours from the individual contracts.</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0abgn7s" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_192hz16" targetRef="TextAnnotation_1xdnwrs" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0hhrrc0">
      <bpmn:text>Deviating target working hours (ASZ)</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0ok266e" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_1bhzzu7" targetRef="TextAnnotation_0hhrrc0" />
    <bpmn:association id="Association_01kahtr" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_178uzcg" targetRef="TextAnnotation_11k1bz0" />
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0sdi7dr" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_178uzcg" targetRef="TextAnnotation_0pui5wv" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0osmpmi">
      <bpmn:text>Reasons for deviating target working hours can include, for example, restrictions on part-time work for pregnant employees.</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0zdgajk" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_1bhzzu7" targetRef="TextAnnotation_0osmpmi" />

assessedActivities.name: Emit invoice
assessedActivities.reason: Emit invoice is a routine administrative step with no modeled exceptions, supporting criteria 5 and 9. However, the model specifies neither an invoicing application nor a digital invoice channel, so UI-based RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Receive Payment
assessedActivities.reason: Receive Payment has one modeled continuation and no exception paths, supporting criterion 9. The payment channel and any software interaction are unspecified, so the model does not establish that RPA can perform this activity.

assessedActivities.name: Confirm order
assessedActivities.reason: Confirm order is a routine confirmation after payment and shipment synchronize, with no modeled exceptions, supporting criteria 5 and 9. No application or digital communication channel is identified, leaving RPA feasibility unsupported.

assessedActivities.name: Archieve order
assessedActivities.reason: Archieve order is a routine filing step with a single path to completion, supporting criteria 5 and 9. The model does not identify a digital archive or distinguish electronic filing from paper filing, so RPA feasibility cannot be determined.

assessedActivities.reason: Preparing a blister is physical work rather than interaction with an application's user interface. The activity has a single modeled continuation and no local exception paths (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: Run test with printed folding box
assessedActivities.reason: The test involves a physical printed folding box, with no modeled software interface through which RPA could execute it. Only one continuation and no local exceptions are shown (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: Check reject entry in MSR
assessedActivities.reason: The following gateway defines a simple entry-existence check with two outcomes, supporting criteria 2, 5, and 9. However, the model does not identify MSR as a digital application or establish an accessible software interface, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Check settings
assessedActivities.reason: The model shows a single return path to repeat preparation (criterion 9), but does not specify the settings, checking rules, or whether they are accessed through software. This is insufficient to establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Admit patient
assessedActivities.reason: The activity produces a Patient record, but the model does not specify software use, digital data, or admission rules. Its context is insufficient to establish RPA feasibility or any criterion.

assessedActivities.name: Perform initial examination
assessedActivities.reason: Examining the patient is a clinical activity rather than a demonstrated software-interface task. The associated Patient record does not establish digital inputs or rule-based execution.

assessedActivities.name: Take blood sample
assessedActivities.reason: Taking a blood sample requires physical work on the patient and cannot be performed by an RPA software robot. The model provides no evidence establishing any of the criteria.

assessedActivities.name: X-ray patient
assessedActivities.reason: This activity involves physically imaging the patient, not merely interacting with application interfaces. The preceding order check does not establish rules or software interactions for performing the activity itself.

assessedActivities.name: Perform blood test
assessedActivities.reason: Following Take blood sample, this activity represents testing a physical specimen rather than a software-only operation. No execution rules, digital inputs, or application interactions are specified.

assessedActivities.name: Create blood test report
assessedActivities.reason: The report contributes to the Patient record, but neither digital test results nor a structured reporting template is specified. The model does not establish whether report creation is routine transcription or requires clinical interpretation, so RPA feasibility is undetermined.

assessedActivities.name: Create X-ray report
assessedActivities.reason: The model does not establish that creating the report avoids clinical image interpretation or follows unambiguous reporting rules. Its Patient record output also does not establish software use or digital data availability.

assessedActivities.name: Perform final examination
assessedActivities.reason: A final patient examination is a clinical activity, not an identified software-interface operation. Access to the Patient record does not demonstrate rule-based execution or remove the need for examining the patient.

assessedActivities.name: Write final report
assessedActivities.reason: The Patient record and Final report have no specified digital format or structure, and no report-generation rules are supplied. The model therefore does not establish criteria supporting automated report writing through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Issue prescription
assessedActivities.reason: The model does not distinguish clinical prescribing decisions from routine issuance of an already determined prescription. Neither prescribing rules nor an electronic prescribing application is specified, leaving RPA feasibility unsupported.

activities.reason: Commision ware prepares available goods for shipment in the Stock lane, indicating routine physical order-picking work. Criterion 5 does not make that physical activity executable through software interfaces.

activities.name: update inventory
activities.reason: Update inventory records article ID and amount in a Database alongside shipment, supporting human software use and routine structured record maintenance. RPA can perform the recording, but the model does not establish that every required input is digital.

activities.name: update inventory
activities.reason: Update inventory follows completed shipment or newly stocked goods and represents routine inventory record maintenance. The neighboring database-backed inventory update supports inferring RPA suitability, but this activity has no direct data or application associations.

activities.name: buy ware
activities.reason: Buy ware records article ID and amount in a Database, supporting software use and structured data. However, supplier selection and purchase execution are unspecified, so automation of the whole purchasing activity cannot be established.

activities.name: send in stock
activities.reason: Send in stock moves purchased ware into Stock before commissioning, indicating routine physical goods handling. It cannot be performed by RPA through application interfaces.

activities.name: buy new assortment
activities.reason: Buy new assortment follows marketing advice, but no purchasing rules, structured purchase inputs or software interactions are specified. The model does not establish an RPA-executable procedure.

activities.name: send in stock
activities.reason: Send in stock follows buying a new assortment and precedes inventory updating, indicating routine physical movement of goods into stock. RPA cannot execute that physical movement.

activities.name: analyze the customers
activities.reason: Analyze the customers is an abstract market-research activity without specified analysis rules, data sources or software interactions. Neither a non-interpretive procedure nor RPA suitability is established.

activities.name:
analyze
competitor
activities.reason: Analyze competitor has no defined analytical method or associated digital inputs. Its market-research context does not establish rule-based processing suitable for RPA.

activities.name: analyze  general market characteristics
activities.reason: Analyze general market characteristics specifies neither a deterministic method nor software-based data handling. The model does not establish that this broad analytical activity avoids complex interpretation or can be executed with RPA.

activities.name: determine sales and inventory
activities.reason: Determine sales and inventory uses the Database populated with order, purchase and inventory records, supporting digital structured inputs and software use by the analyst. In this context, determining recorded sales and stock levels is routine data retrieval or aggregation suitable for RPA.

activities.name: determine result of market research
activities.reason: Determine result of market research synthesizes the preceding analyses without specified evaluation rules or data formats. The model does not establish a routine, software-executable procedure.

activities.name:
prepare optimization
report
activities.reason: Prepare optimization report combines research results with sales and inventory findings, but no report template or optimization rules are supplied. The model does not establish that report preparation is mechanical rather than interpretive.

activities.name: advice for buying new assortment
activities.reason: Advice for buying new assortment develops purchasing recommendations from the optimization report without specified decision rules. No evidence establishes non-interpretive work or an RPA-executable advisory procedure.

activities.name: advice for selling stock ware with low price
activities.reason: Advice for selling stock ware with low price has no defined discount thresholds, selection rules or software procedure. Its recommendation-making role therefore cannot be classified as automatable from the model.

assessedActivities.name: Check medical report

assessedActivities.reason: The typist's position after dictation supports interpreting this as transcription rather than creative report composition (criterion 5), with only the initial and revision paths modeled (criterion 9). expectedNamesWithIds.name: Submit application for acceptance as doctoral candidate
Carry out equivalence assessment, including grade if applicable
Send acceptance with request to enroll

actualNamesWithIds.name: Submit application for acceptance as doctoral candidate
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The candidate submits the application through the CMS, supporting criterion 1. The supervisor and topic are already determined, so submission rather than creation of academic content is a routine action suitable for RPA (criterion 5).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Inform applicant about acceptance
actualNamesWithIds.reason: This activity communicates an acceptance decision already reached in the CMS-supported process rather than making that decision (criterion 5). The context supports automating the routine notification with RPA, although the communication channel is not specified.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send acceptance with request to enroll
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The acceptance decision precedes this activity, and the message has a prescribed purpose: communicating acceptance and requesting enrollment (criterion 5). In the CMS-supported administrative context, this routine communication is suitable for RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Register doctoral candidate
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Registration follows acceptance and the candidate's enrollment choice, making it an administrative recording action rather than an academic decision (criterion 5). The CMS-based process and the restriction of subsequent data maintenance to the doctoral office support inferring suitability for RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Enroll doctoral candidate
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The Office of Academic Affairs performs enrollment using Campus Core and the CMS, and the annotation describes transferring accepted applicant records through an interface, supporting criteria 1 and 7. This post-acceptance administrative processing is suitable for RPA (criterion 5), without assuming that the existing interface transfer itself requires a robot.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Submit application for admission to doctoral examination
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The doctoral candidate submits the application using the CMS, supporting criterion 1. Submission, rather than preparation or evaluation, is a routine operation with no modeled alternatives and can be performed through the application's interface.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Open procedure and inform doctoral candidate about deadlines
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The doctoral office performs this administrative activity in the CMS, with deadlines and examiner requirements explicitly governed by doctoral regulations. Opening the procedure and communicating prescribed deadlines are suitable for interface automation; the model does not establish that the regulations are unambiguous or stable over time.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Inform doctoral candidate about missing documents
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The activity communicates the result of the preceding CMS-supported completeness check rather than making a new judgment. In this administrative context, RPA can convey the identified missing documents, with one modeled continuation to resubmission.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Create report
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Staff unit QBR creates the report using the CMS at the completion stage, supporting inference of an application-based administrative reporting activity suitable for RPA. assessedActivities.name: Submit required documents
assessedActivities.reason: Submitting existing documents does not itself require creativity and has one modeled continuation. However, unlike the application submission, this activity has no specified software channel or digital document format, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct of the doctoral examination procedure
assessedActivities.reason: The CMS annotation supports human software use, and the process models two examination outcomes. However, conducting the examination is broader than operating the CMS, and no executable assessment rules are provided to establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Publish dissertation
assessedActivities.reason: Publication has one modeled continuation, but the model specifies neither a publication application nor an electronic publication method. The abstract activity therefore lacks sufficient context to establish automation through software interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Submit application for Deutschlandstipendium

assessedActivities.name: Complete filling out the application
assessedActivities.reason: The CMS annotation supports human software use (criterion 1), but the associated output explicitly includes printing and signing the application. This physical component prevents automation of the entire activity through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Attach the required documents for the application
assessedActivities.reason: Attaching documents is a noncreative operation (criterion 5), but its position between printing/signing and postal dispatch indicates physical document assembly. RPA cannot perform that physical work.

assessedActivities.name: Send application by post
assessedActivities.reason: Postal dispatch does not inherently require creativity (criterion 5), but it requires physical handling and delivery. The CMS annotation does not make postal dispatch executable through software interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Scan barcode on application documents
assessedActivities.reason: The CMS retrieves structured applicant data using the barcode, with access explicitly blocked until scanning occurs, supporting criteria 1, 2, 4, 5 and 7. expectedNamesWithIds.name: Mark scholarship recipients, reserves, and rejected applicants

actualNamesWithIds.name: Adjust Excel list
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Updating the Excel list to reflect the three cohorts already determined by the committee is a straightforward software-based recording task using structured data (criteria 1, 2, 5 and 7). RPA can perform these updates without making the selection decisions.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Mark scholarship recipients, reserves, and rejected applicants
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The department records the already determined Excel classifications in the CMS, supporting human software use, unambiguous status transfer and no complex interpretation (criteria 1, 2 and 5). The classifications are structured and digitally available in the adjusted Excel list (criteria 7 and 8).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Enter data into the CMS
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Departmental entry of bank details, consents and eligibility-related data into the CMS supports human software use, routine transcription and structured system data (criteria 1, 5 and 7). The data-entry portion is suitable for RPA, although the informal incoming information does not establish criterion 8.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Instruct payment to scholarship recipients
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The accounting department uses SAP to instruct payments for already approved recipients, supporting human software use and routine processing of structured payment data (criteria 1, 5 and 7). RPA can perform the software instruction step, but the incoming paper notice means that digital availability of all inputs is not established.

assessedActivities.reason: Although results have been recorded in the CMS, the model does not specify a letter template, generation rules or a digital delivery channel. It therefore does not establish that the complete creation and sending activity can be performed through software interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Inform themselves via the alumni portal website
assessedActivities.reason: The alumnus accesses digital information through a website, supporting criteria 1 and 8. However, becoming informed involves human understanding, and the model specifies no retrieval or processing rules that an RPA robot could execute in its place.

assessedActivities.name: Inform themselves about current topics
assessedActivities.reason: The alumnus becomes informed after receiving an email or letter, so neither software use nor exclusively digital inputs are established. No rule-based operation is specified that could replace this human understanding activity.

assessedActivities.name: Update information on the website
assessedActivities.reason: Updating a website by the Alumni Office supports human use of software under criterion 1. The model does not distinguish mechanical publication from editorial revision or specify how updates are determined, so automation of the complete activity cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Send newsletter
assessedActivities.reason: Sending, rather than composing, a newsletter indicates a noncreative dispatch operation under criterion 5. However, the model identifies neither a digital delivery channel nor an application used for this activity, leaving UI-based RPA feasibility unsupported.

assessedActivities.name: Inform members
assessedActivities.reason: The CMS annotation supports software use by the Alumni Office under criterion 1. However, the email-or-letter outcome and absence of specified communication steps leave it unclear whether the entire activity can be performed through software interfaces.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Search for other members
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The alumnus searches in the CMS (criterion 1), and the subsequent check for a requested member indicates a routine lookup suitable for RPA rather than creative work (criterion 5). The modeled outcomes are limited to member found or not found (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Add member to personal contact list
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The CMS annotation and preceding member-found check support a human software operation with a clear action: add the found member to the personal contact list (criteria 1, 2, and 5). actualNamesWithIds.name: Create selection list of courses / modules within area of responsibility
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The Dean of Studies creates a list of course/module records in CMS, supporting human software use and structured digital data. Compiling the list within the stated responsibility scope is a noncreative software operation suitable for RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Import of courses to be evaluated into internal database
actualNamesWithIds.reason: QBR staff use LVE-helper to import the courses previously marked in CMS into an internal database. This is a noncreative transfer of structured digital records suitable for RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Import of courses to be evaluated into EvaSys
actualNamesWithIds.reason: QBR staff import the previously selected digital course records into EvaSys. The software-based transfer uses structured data and does not itself require creative interpretation, supporting RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Confirm that evaluation results are available
actualNamesWithIds.reason: After analysis in EvaSys, QBR staff confirm result availability using LVE-helper. Confirming the availability of digital results is a simple, unambiguous status operation suitable for RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Acknowledges results
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The lecturer acknowledges received digital results using EvaSys, supporting a simple software-based acknowledgment suitable for RPA. The subsequent verbal presentation is modeled separately and is not part of this automation assessment.

assessedActivities.name: Create selection list of courses / modules within area of responsibility
assessedActivities.reason: The Dean of Studies creates a list of course/module records in CMS, supporting human software use and structured digital data. Compiling the list within the stated responsibility scope is a noncreative software operation suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Mark courses / modules to be evaluated
assessedActivities.reason: The Dean of Studies marks structured course/module records in CMS, supporting criteria 1, 7 and 8. However, the model provides no criteria for deciding which courses to evaluate, so automation of the selection decision is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Import of courses to be evaluated into internal database
assessedActivities.reason: QBR staff use LVE-helper to import the courses previously marked in CMS into an internal database. This is a noncreative transfer of structured digital records suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Import of courses to be evaluated into EvaSys
assessedActivities.reason: QBR staff import the previously selected digital course records into EvaSys. The software-based transfer uses structured data and does not itself require creative interpretation, supporting RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Create evaluation materials
assessedActivities.reason: The annotation identifies return envelopes and evaluation forms, followed by dispatch of those materials. This includes physical preparation, and no purely digital creation procedure is specified.

assessedActivities.name: Distribute evaluation forms in course
assessedActivities.reason: Distributing the dispatched paper forms in a course is a routine, noncreative action, supporting criterion 5. It is nevertheless physical work rather than application interaction and cannot be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Fill out evaluation form
assessedActivities.reason: Students provide their own evaluations on forms that are subsequently collected and scanned. The activity involves personal judgment and paper-based input rather than an automatable software operation.

assessedActivities.name: Collect evaluation forms
assessedActivities.reason: Collecting paper evaluation forms is routine physical work; the LVE-helper annotation additionally indicates software-based feedback that the course has been evaluated. Although this supports human software use for the feedback component, RPA cannot perform the collection activity as a whole.

assessedActivities.name: Scan and validate evaluation forms
assessedActivities.reason: QBR staff use EvaSys, supporting criterion 1, but the activity begins with returned physical forms that must be scanned. Physical handling and unspecified validation requirements prevent establishing full RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Analysis of evaluation forms
assessedActivities.reason: QBR staff analyze forms in EvaSys after scanning and validation, supporting human software use and digital inputs. The model does not specify whether analysis is a predefined software operation or requires interpretation, so RPA feasibility is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Confirm that evaluation results are available
assessedActivities.reason: After analysis in EvaSys, QBR staff confirm result availability using LVE-helper. Confirming the availability of digital results is a simple, unambiguous status operation suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Retrieve evaluation results and clean them
assessedActivities.reason: The EvaSys and LVE-helper annotations establish software use and digitally available results. Retrieval could be automated, but no cleaning rules are provided, so feasibility for the complete activity cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Acknowledges results
assessedActivities.reason: The lecturer acknowledges received digital results using EvaSys, supporting a simple software-based acknowledgment suitable for RPA. The subsequent verbal presentation is modeled separately and is not part of this automation assessment.

assessedActivities.reason: The Office of Academic Affairs uses the CMS with structured examination assignments and PF/WP classifications (criteria 1 and 7). However, the model supplies no rules for selecting a proposed date, so automation of the complete activity is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Check whether the examination is assigned to the correct examiner
assessedActivities.reason: The Examination Coordinator checks examination assignments in the CMS, supporting criteria 1 and 7. The model does not specify how the correct examiner is determined or provide an authoritative reference for automated comparison.

assessedActivities.name: Create proposed date for the non-interdisciplinary compulsory examination
assessedActivities.reason: The Examination Coordinator creates a structured date in the CMS (criteria 1 and 7). No scheduling rules or required availability information are specified, so selecting the proposed date cannot confidently be classified as RPA-feasible.

assessedActivities.name: Create proposed date for the elective compulsory examination
assessedActivities.reason: The CMS annotation and coordinator lane support human software use and structured date data (criteria 1 and 7). The model does not explain how a suitable date is selected, leaving automation of the proposal unsupported.

assessedActivities.name: Check date
assessedActivities.reason: The activity checks a structured date proposed through the CMS (criterion 7). However, the examiner's acceptance rules and any additional information needed for confirmation are unspecified, preventing a supported RPA decision.

assessedActivities.name: Correct date
assessedActivities.reason: The correction concerns structured date data (criterion 7), but the model gives neither correction rules nor a software interaction for the examiner. Choosing a replacement date therefore cannot be established as automatable.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Record prerequisite achievement as completed
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The examiner records a defined completion status in the CMS after the prerequisite decision, supporting human software use, an unambiguous update, and structured data (criteria 1, 2, 5, 7). This routine recording step has a single modeled continuation and can be performed through the CMS interface (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Record prerequisite achievement as not completed
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The examiner uses the CMS to record a predefined negative completion status after the prerequisite decision (criteria 1, 2, 5, 7). RPA can perform this recording without making the prerequisite assessment; subsequent document submission may trigger reassessment.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Release oral examination for registration - NO date
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Academic Affairs uses the CMS to release an offered oral examination for registration explicitly without a date, providing a defined, noncreative software action (criteria 1, 2, 5). The release itself has no modeled alternative execution path and is suitable for RPA (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Create and send withdrawal notices
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Academic Affairs creates and sends the notices using the CMS following the final-failure decision, supporting software-based execution suitable for RPA (criterion 1). The activity leads directly to withdrawal with no modeled exceptions, although notice templates and composition rules are not specified (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Register for prerequisite achievement
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The student registers through the CMS after the process identifies that a prerequisite is required, supporting a routine software interaction without creative assessment (criteria 1, 5). The registration has one modeled continuation and is suitable for RPA (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Register for examination - NO date
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The student performs registration in the CMS, explicitly without entering an examination date, making it a routine software action suitable for RPA (criteria 1, 5). Registration has one modeled continuation; agreement on a date is handled separately afterward (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Student registers for the repeat examination
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The student registers in the CMS, which explicitly checks examination-regulation rules for repeat examinations, free attempts, and closed examinations, supporting software use and system-applied rules (criteria 1, 2, 4). RPA can submit this routine registration while leaving those checks to the CMS; only one continuation is modeled (criteria 5, 9).

assessedActivities.name: Inform student
assessedActivities.reason: The Office of Academic Affairs uses CMS to notify the student of a degree already generated there and convey specified instructions. This supports human software use, routine communication without complex interpretation, and digital availability of the notification content.

assessedActivities.name: Check information
assessedActivities.reason: The student checks information before choosing or changing certificate-relevant assignments, but no validation rules or comparison source are specified. The model therefore does not establish that this review can be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Re-send information
assessedActivities.reason: The office re-sends existing information through CMS following the timer and loop-count condition. This provides a rule-based trigger for a routine software action using already digital information.

assessedActivities.name: Edit certificate-relevant information
assessedActivities.reason: The student edits assignments and subject selections in CMS, supporting human software use and structured data. However, deciding which assignments to retain or change and which additional subjects to include requires student choices for which no automatable rules are supplied.

assessedActivities.name: Create certificate, degree certificate, diploma supplement
assessedActivities.reason: The preceding CMS confirmation and specified diploma-supplement fields support interpreting this as routine document preparation from structured academic information. RPA can populate these documents, although the model does not establish templates, stable rules, or digital availability of every required field.

assessedActivities.name: Sign certificate, degree certificate, diploma supplement
assessedActivities.reason: Signing is assigned to the PA Chair, with no software or digital-signature mechanism specified. In the context of documents subsequently collected or posted, the model does not support execution through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Sign certificate, degree certificate, diploma supplement
assessedActivities.reason: Signing is assigned to the Dean, with no software or digital-signature mechanism specified. The subsequent physical document distribution does not establish an RPA-compatible signing action.

assessedActivities.name: Create certifications and cover letter, store a copy in Regisafe
assessedActivities.reason: The CMS and Regisafe annotations identify software used by the office for document preparation and copy storage. The context supports routine document production and filing through application interfaces, without establishing that all inputs are digital or that detailed interaction rules are stable.

assessedActivities.name: Collect documents
assessedActivities.reason: The alternative to registered-mail delivery is physical collection by the student. Although collection does not require creativity or complex interpretation, it cannot be performed by a software robot through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Send documents by registered mail
assessedActivities.reason: Registered-mail delivery involves physical dispatch of the documents rather than a purely software-based action. Its routine nature supports criterion 5 but does not make the complete activity automatable with RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Recall patient's data
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Reception retrieves structured patient data already stored digitally in SAP/R3, a routine software operation suitable for RPA. The activity has a single modeled continuation and no modeled exceptions.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Print badges with personal data
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Printing badges from structured personal data in SAP/R3 is a routine reception software operation whose print command can be performed through an application interface. No separate physical handling or exceptional paths are modeled.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Print treatment contract 4 times
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The activity specifies an unambiguous four-copy printing instruction and uses structured digital patient data from SAP/R3. This routine reception printing operation is suitable for RPA, with subsequent contract delivery modeled separately.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Print discharge papers
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Reception prints discharge papers using structured digital patient data from SAP/R3, supporting a routine application operation suitable for RPA. The activity contains no modeled physical handling or alternative execution paths.

assessedActivities.name: Recall patient's data
assessedActivities.reason: Reception retrieves structured patient data already stored digitally in SAP/R3, a routine software operation suitable for RPA. The activity has a single modeled continuation and no modeled exceptions.

assessedActivities.name: Check and complement patient's data
assessedActivities.reason: Reception checks recalled patient fields and updates SAP/R3, supporting human software use and structured data. The model supplies neither validation rules nor the source of supplementary information, so automation of the complete activity is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Create magnetic card
assessedActivities.reason: The activity uses structured digital patient data from SAP/R3 for routine card creation. Its output is a physical magnetic card, and the model does not establish a software-controlled creation mechanism that RPA could operate.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Approve report
actualNamesWithIds.reason: In the software-supported clerk workflow, this activity executes the approval branch after the outcome gateway and leads directly to the approved end state. Recording that selected outcome is a noncreative software action with one modeled continuation (criteria 1, 5 and 9); this does not imply that the preceding approval decision can be automated.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Return report to applicant
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Within the software-supported workflow, returning the report to its applicant is a routing action after the outcome branch has been selected (criteria 1 and 5). It has one modeled continuation, ending with the report requiring revision (criterion 9), so RPA can execute the return.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Forward the report to another clerk
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The software-supported process context permits interpreting this as executing a report handoff rather than reviewing its merits (criteria 1 and 5). activities.name: delegates task to support embloyee

activities.name: document Proces start
activities.reason: Recording the start of the digital process after establishing its ID is a noncreative system operation using digital process information, supporting criteria 5 and 8. Its single modeled completion path supports criterion 9, and the recording operation is suitable for RPA.

activities.name: save data
activities.reason: The system saves collected form data into a record with problem description, version and prioritization fields, supporting criteria 5, 7 and 8. This digital persistence operation has one completion path, supporting criterion 9, and can be reproduced through an application interface.

activities.name: remind support employee
activities.reason: The first-level escalation timer explicitly triggers a system reminder to the support employee, providing a clear trigger and a noncreative digital action under criteria 2, 5 and 8. The single reminder path supports criterion 9 and is suitable for RPA.

activities.name: close ticket
activities.reason: The parallel join defines when the system closes the digital ticket, supporting criterion 2. Closing that structured record is a noncreative digital operation with one terminal path, supporting criteria 5, 7, 8 and 9 and suitability for RPA.

activities.name: fill formular
activities.reason: The employee completes a form for subsequent system storage, supporting software use, structured fields and one completion path under criteria 1, 7 and 9. activities.name: determine email

activities.name: determine customer nr.

activities.name: categorize problem
activities.reason: The problem has already been saved digitally, and the following gateway provides only two prioritization paths, supporting criteria 8 and 9. No category definitions or classification rules establish that categorization can avoid complex interpretation.

activities.name: change prioritization
activities.reason: Prioritization is explicitly part of the saved digital record, and the change has one completion path, supporting criteria 7, 8 and 9. The model does not specify how the replacement priority is chosen, so automating the entire activity is not established.

activities.name: problem viewing
activities.reason: The employee reviews the previously saved digital problem before checking the database, supporting criteria 1, 8 and 9. The context suggests substantive review rather than merely opening a screen, and no rules define that review.

activities.name: check DB for known problem
activities.reason: The employee explicitly checks a database against a digitally recorded problem, supporting criteria 1 and 8. activities.name: determine support employee
activities.reason: There is one modeled completion path to the assignment email, supporting criterion 9. No staff directory, availability data or employee-selection rules establish an automatable assignment decision.

activities.name: capture working time
activities.reason: Recording time values is noncreative and structured, and has one modeled completion path, supporting criteria 5, 7 and 9. The model does not identify a digital time source or time-recording application needed to establish RPA feasibility.

activities.name: write summary
activities.reason: The summary has one modeled completion path, supporting criterion 9. Even on the known-problem branch, no template or composition rules establish noncreative summary generation.

activities.name: write e-mail

assessedActivities.name: Adjust cost accounting
assessedActivities.reason: The surrounding QIS settlement workflow supports interpreting this as a clerk's software-based activity. However, the model provides no adjustment rules or details sufficient to determine whether the accounting decisions can be automated.

assessedActivities.name: Verify bank details
assessedActivities.reason: The bank register card in the QIS workflow supports human software use and structured bank data. No verification rules or comparison source are specified, so the model does not establish that the verification can be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Enter bank account details
assessedActivities.reason: Entering structured bank account details in the clerk's software-based settlement workflow is a noncreative data-entry operation suitable for RPA. The source of those details is unspecified, so availability of all inputs in digital form is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Automatically adjust reference
assessedActivities.reason: The annotation specifies the exact digital reference change from Q to E, making this a deterministic, noncreative update of structured data. Although already described as automatic rather than human-performed, the same update is feasible through the interface used by the alternative manual activity.

assessedActivities.name: Manually adjust reference
assessedActivities.reason: The clerk changes the QIS reference from Q to E according to an explicit rule, using structured digital data without creative interpretation. Here, manual adjustment denotes human interaction with the software, not physical or handwritten work.

assessedActivities.name: View billing data
assessedActivities.reason: The annotation identifies the overnight stay register card as the location of the billing data in the software workflow. Opening and displaying these structured digital records is suitable for RPA; the activity does not specify any interpretive assessment.

assessedActivities.name: Make further adjustments
assessedActivities.reason: The annotation clarifies the otherwise abstract activity as approving all register cards in the travel expense report. As modeled, this is an unconditional software operation on digital records rather than a discretionary approval assessment.

assessedActivities.name: Perform booking
assessedActivities.reason: The annotation describes concrete software operations: reading and writing the HÜL table and assigning posting and HÜL fields, supporting RPA interaction with structured digital records. Assignment rules are not supplied, so unambiguous rules and absence of complex interpretation are not established.

assessedActivities.name: Create report
assessedActivities.reason: The surrounding settlement workflow supports software-based report creation by the clerk. However, no report template, content requirements, or generation operation is specified, so the model does not establish whether creation is routine or requires original composition.

assessedActivities.name: Check creditworthiness
assessedActivities.reason: The Credit department system annotation supports human use of software under criterion 1. However, no creditworthiness rules or decision thresholds are supplied, so the model does not establish that RPA can perform the assessment.

assessedActivities.name: Note results
assessedActivities.reason: Recording results already produced by Check creditworthiness supports criterion 5. The model does not specify whether the results are recorded in software or on paper, leaving RPA feasibility undetermined.

assessedActivities.name: Forward application to business practices department
assessedActivities.reason: Forwarding to the explicitly named department supports criteria 2 and 5. No electronic transfer mechanism or digital application is identified for this handoff.

assessedActivities.name: Check customer requirements
assessedActivities.reason: The activity determines whether the standard contract needs adjustment, but the model supplies neither assessment rules nor a software interaction. It therefore does not establish that this potentially interpretive check can be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Adjust standard contract
assessedActivities.reason: The Business Practices system annotation supports criterion 1. However, the model does not define how customer requirements translate into contract changes, so rule-based UI automation cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Attach special conditions
assessedActivities.reason: Attaching conditions after the contract adjustment is a routine assembly operation, supporting criterion 5. The model does not establish that the attachment operation or the conditions themselves are digital.

assessedActivities.name: Forward application to pricing specialist
assessedActivities.reason: The fixed recipient supports an unambiguous, noncreative forwarding operation under criteria 2 and 5. The model does not specify a software-mediated handoff that RPA could execute.

assessedActivities.name: Enter information

assessedActivities.name: Determine appropriate interest rate
assessedActivities.reason: The model provides no pricing formula, decision table, or software system for determining an appropriate rate. It does not establish that the pricing specialist's assessment can be replaced by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Note interest rate
assessedActivities.reason: Recording an already determined numerical interest rate supports criteria 5 and 7. However, the model does not identify a digital recording medium or software interface.

assessedActivities.name: Forward application to administrative group
assessedActivities.reason: The explicitly specified destination supports criteria 2 and 5 for this routine handoff. Its transmission medium is unspecified, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Create offer letter
assessedActivities.reason: Although the letter follows contract and pricing preparation, the model specifies neither a template nor composition rules or a software system. It therefore does not establish that letter creation is a routine digital operation suitable for RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Create customer as prospect
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Creating a prospect in CRM by field service supports human software use and routine entry of structured customer data (criteria 1, 5 and 7). This is a suitable application-entry activity for RPA, although the model does not establish that all input data are digital.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Create customer record
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Creating customer records in CRM and AX supports human software use and routine structured-data entry (criteria 1, 5 and 7), which RPA can perform through application interfaces. The travel-report annotation does not establish that all required inputs are digital or that entry rules are stable.

assessedActivities.name: Process request
assessedActivities.reason: The annotation describes initial research for suitable offers, without selection rules or identified software inputs. The model does not establish rule-based execution or sufficient context for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Create customer as prospect
assessedActivities.reason: Creating a prospect in CRM by field service supports human software use and routine entry of structured customer data (criteria 1, 5 and 7). This is a suitable application-entry activity for RPA, although the model does not establish that all input data are digital.

assessedActivities.name: Present portfolio
assessedActivities.reason: Presenting suitable products, logistics and prices to the customer has no specified presentation rules or software channel. The model does not establish a predictable, non-interpretive activity that RPA could perform.

assessedActivities.name: Visit and advise customer
assessedActivities.reason: The activity involves a customer visit and expert services such as teardown, design and testing. Physical attendance and expert advice cannot be performed through application user interfaces alone.

assessedActivities.name: Create concept
assessedActivities.reason: Creating a concept after customer advice is not supported by defined rules, templates or software data. The model does not establish the absence of creativity or complex interpretation required by criterion 5.

assessedActivities.name: Write travel report
assessedActivities.reason: Writing the report into CRM supports human software use (criterion 1). However, documenting the visit is not shown as routine transcription from available digital inputs, so automation of the report-writing activity is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Present concept
assessedActivities.reason: The activity communicates a concept to the customer, but no software channel or standardized presentation procedure is specified. The context is insufficient to infer RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Create customer record
assessedActivities.reason: Creating customer records in CRM and AX supports human software use and routine structured-data entry (criteria 1, 5 and 7), which RPA can perform through application interfaces. assessedActivities.name: Classify Claim
assessedActivities.reason: Classify Claim is assigned to an expert, but the model specifies neither classification rules nor software use. The context does not establish that classification avoids complex interpretation or can be performed through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Receive Insurance Claim
assessedActivities.reason: Receive Insurance Claim describes receipt rather than interpretation, supporting criterion 5. However, the model does not identify a digital submission channel or an application through which RPA could receive the claim.

assessedActivities.name: Examine Damage History
assessedActivities.reason: Examine Damage History has no specified examination rules, data format, or software system. The model does not establish that the examination is rule-based rather than interpretive, or that its inputs are digitally accessible.

assessedActivities.name: Calculate Insurance Sum
assessedActivities.reason: Calculate Insurance Sum describes a numerical calculation, supporting criterion 5, but the model supplies no formula or evidence of digital inputs and application access. Consequently, it does not establish that RPA can execute the calculation in this process.

assessedActivities.name: Contace Garage
assessedActivities.reason: Contace Garage specifies neither the communication channel nor the content or rules for the interaction. The model therefore does not establish a predictable, non-interpretive communication activity accessible through software.

assessedActivities.name: Decide on Payment
assessedActivities.reason: Decide on Payment follows the calculation and garage contact, but no payment decision rules are provided. Neither the absence of complex judgment nor software-based execution is established.

assessedActivities.name: Send Letter to Customer
assessedActivities.reason: Send Letter to Customer describes dispatch rather than creative composition, supporting criterion 5. The model does not specify electronic delivery or a software interface, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Initiate Payment
assessedActivities.reason: Initiate Payment follows a separate payment decision, supporting criterion 5 for execution rather than judgment. However, the finance lane alone does not establish a payment application, digital payment details, or an interface that RPA could operate.

assessedActivities.name: Suspend internet
assessedActivities.reason: The model specifies suspension following notification that money was not received, supporting a clear trigger and a noncreative action (criteria 2 and 5). It does not establish whether suspension uses a software interface or requires other operational work, so RPA feasibility is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Close account
assessedActivities.reason: Continued nonpayment provides a clear trigger for a routine closure action, with no alternative execution path shown (criteria 2, 5 and 9). The model does not describe the closure procedure or establish an application interface through which RPA could perform it.

assessedActivities.name: Send payment
assessedActivities.reason: Sending payment after a late-fee notification is a noncreative transaction (criterion 5). Neither the payment channel nor a software-based execution method is specified, and the subsequent flow explicitly permits incomplete payment.

assessedActivities.name: Send payment
assessedActivities.reason: This payment submission follows an incomplete-payment notification and has a single modeled completion path, supporting criteria 5 and 9. The model does not establish whether the customer submits payment digitally or through a channel accessible to RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Debit money
assessedActivities.reason: The Day 7 trigger defines when the bank performs this routine debit (criteria 2 and 5), while the following gateway explicitly allows transaction failure. No banking application, digital input source or user-interface operation is established, so RPA feasibility remains uncertain.

assessedActivities.name: Debit money
assessedActivities.reason: The retry on Day 9 after the earlier failure has an explicit trigger and involves a routine debit (criteria 2 and 5). The model shows another possible failure but does not establish an application interface or digital inputs for RPA execution.

assessedActivities.name: Charge late fee
assessedActivities.reason: Charging a late fee on Day 10 after unsuccessful debit attempts is a clearly triggered, noncreative action with one modeled continuation (criteria 2, 5 and 9). The fee calculation and means of posting the charge are unspecified, preventing a supported RPA decision.

assessedActivities.name: Receive payment
assessedActivities.reason: Receiving the customer's payment is noncreative (criterion 5), but the message flow does not establish a digital payment channel. The model also does not identify an application operation that an RPA robot could perform rather than merely waiting for funds.

assessedActivities.name: Check payment
assessedActivities.reason: The Day 14 check determines whether payment is complete, providing a clear, noncreative check with two defined outcomes (criteria 2, 5 and 9). The model supplies no payment-record source or software interface, so the ability to perform the check through RPA is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Receive payment
assessedActivities.reason: Receiving a further payment after an incomplete-payment notification does not itself require creativity (criterion 5). The payment medium and any application-based receipt or recording operation are unspecified, leaving RPA feasibility uncertain.

assessedActivities.name: Check payment
assessedActivities.reason: The Day 30 check has a clear payment-completeness question and two defined outcomes, supporting criteria 2, 5 and 9. No digital payment-record source or application interaction is identified, so the model does not establish that RPA can execute the check.

result.name: Fill in request form for further examinations

assessedActivities.name: Obtain consent for anesthesia
assessedActivities.reason: Obtaining consent involves patient agreement, not merely producing the Consent document. The 24-hour requirement specifies timing but does not establish an unambiguous, software-executable consent procedure or digital inputs.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct anamnesis and physical examination
assessedActivities.reason: This activity includes a physical examination by the anesthetist and clinical interpretation. It cannot be performed through application user interfaces, and the model provides no evidence supporting the feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Fill in request form for further examinations
assessedActivities.reason: The request form supports structured data use (criterion 7). However, neither the Kardex nor the Order file is identified as digital, and no software interaction or form-completion rules are specified, so the model does not establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Classify patient in ASA
assessedActivities.reason: The anesthetist classifies the patient using examination results, but the model provides no explicit classification rules that eliminate clinical interpretation. It also does not establish digital availability of the results or software use.

assessedActivities.name: Cancel surgery
assessedActivities.reason: Cancellation is described abstractly, with no cancellation procedure, application, or associated digital data. The preceding gateway does not specify decision conditions, so the context is insufficient to establish an RPA-executable activity.

assessedActivities.name: Check pulmunary function
assessedActivities.reason: The nurse performs a clinical function check and produces Pulmunary functions data; this is not modeled as processing existing digital measurements. No software-based procedure or unambiguous checking rules are supplied to support RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Perform ECG
assessedActivities.reason: Performing an ECG is a physical patient-testing activity, rather than an application-user-interface task. The admission-day timing and EKG output do not establish software execution or digital availability of all required inputs.

assessedActivities.name: Examine patient

assessedActivities.name: Present patient on the basis of file.
assessedActivities.reason: The model describes a physician presenting a patient using a patient file, but does not establish software use, digital or structured data, or an unambiguous presentation procedure. None of the criteria is sufficiently supported, and the context does not establish feasibility for UI-based RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Order chemotherapy
assessedActivities.reason: The model places chemotherapy ordering with physicians after patient presentation, without specifying ordering rules or a software interface. It does not establish that this is routine order entry rather than clinical decision-making, so no criteria or RPA feasibility are sufficiently supported.

assessedActivities.reason: The activity checks a specific payment-receipt condition with two modeled outcomes, supporting criteria 2, 5 and 9. However, the model does not identify digital payment records or an application through which RPA could perform the check.

assessedActivities.name: Notify legal department
assessedActivities.reason: The modeled notification to a fixed recipient is a straightforward communication with one execution path, supporting criteria 5 and 9. The message flow does not specify an electronic communication channel or application, so UI-based automation cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Verification of the invoice amount
assessedActivities.reason: Verification of the invoice amount leads to three modeled alternatives, supporting criterion 9's allowance for few alternative paths. Verification rules, data format and application access are unspecified, leaving RPA feasibility unestablished.

assessedActivities.name: File police report
assessedActivities.reason: File police report has one modeled continuation to case handover, supporting criterion 9. The model provides neither report preparation rules nor an electronic filing interface, so it does not establish that RPA can perform the activity.

assessedActivities.name: Issue summary proceedings
assessedActivities.reason: Issue summary proceedings has a single modeled continuation without an exception path, supporting criterion 9. The legal execution requirements and any supporting software are unspecified, preventing a supported RPA classification.

assessedActivities.name: SCHUFA check
assessedActivities.reason: SCHUFA check has one modeled execution path into the parallel join, supporting criterion 9. Its name does not establish the checking rules, digital availability of inputs or a software interface usable by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Review of payment arrears
assessedActivities.reason: Review of payment arrears has one modeled continuation into the parallel join, supporting criterion 9. The model does not define what constitutes a positive review or identify digital records and applications, so automation cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Close the case
assessedActivities.reason: Close the case has a single continuation to informing After Sales, supporting criterion 9. The model does not specify whether closure is a software update or involves other work, so it provides insufficient context to establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Create customer letter regarding blocking
assessedActivities.reason: Create customer letter regarding blocking has one modeled continuation to customer notification, supporting criterion 9. No template, composition rules, digital inputs or document application is specified, so automated letter creation is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Determination of further procedure
assessedActivities.reason: Determination of further procedure has a single modeled continuation to completion, supporting criterion 9. The customer's decision has no specified rules or software context, so the model does not support automating it with RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Print surgery report
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Printing the report immediately after its creation supports a human software operation on an existing digital document, satisfying criteria 1 and 8. Invoking printing requires no clinical interpretation under criterion 5 and can be performed by RPA through the application's interface.

result.name: Print surgery report
result.reasoning: Printing the report immediately after its creation supports a human software operation on an existing digital document, satisfying criteria 1 and 8. Invoking printing requires no clinical interpretation under criterion 5 and can be performed by RPA through the application's interface.

assessedActivities.name: Admit patient
assessedActivities.reason: The model does not specify admission rules, software use, or digital inputs. The MTA lane alone does not establish criterion 1 or sufficient context for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Schedule surgery
assessedActivities.reason: Scheduling follows the surgery decision, but no scheduling rules, application, or digital availability data are specified. Criteria 1, 2, and 8 are therefore unsupported, and RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Perform medical checkup
assessedActivities.reason: This is a physician's clinical examination rather than a software-interface activity. The model provides no evidence of qualifying rules or a noninterpretive digital task.

assessedActivities.name: Discuss anesthesia
assessedActivities.reason: The activity represents a physician's clinical discussion, with no prescribed script or software interaction. Neither rule-based execution nor the absence of complex interpretation is established.

assessedActivities.name: Discuss risks
assessedActivities.reason: A physician discusses clinical risks before the surgery decision. No unambiguous discussion rules or application-based execution are specified to support RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Decide on surgery
assessedActivities.reason: The decision follows medical assessment and clinical discussions, but the model supplies no decision rules. The subsequent gateway does not establish criterion 2 or eliminate the need for clinical interpretation under criterion 5.

assessedActivities.name: Write discharge letter
assessedActivities.reason: The outpatient letter has no specified template, digital source data, or software application. The model does not establish that its clinical content can be produced without complex interpretation.

assessedActivities.name: Check patient record
assessedActivities.reason: The physician's record check has no defined validation rules or specified record format. A patient record alone does not establish structured digital data or software use under criteria 1, 7, and 8.

assessedActivities.name: Discharge patient
assessedActivities.reason: Discharge follows post-surgical care and is assigned to a physician, but no discharge rules or digital administrative operations are specified. The context does not establish an RPA-executable activity.

assessedActivities.name: Write discharge letter
assessedActivities.reason: The surgical ward receives a surgery report after it is printed, which does not establish digital availability of the letter's inputs. No template or rules establish noninterpretive letter generation under criteria 2 and 5.

assessedActivities.name: Admit patient
assessedActivities.reason: The nurse admits the patient before surgical preparation, but the model does not identify a software-based admission operation. No rules or digital inputs establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Prepare patient for surgery
assessedActivities.reason: This is direct patient preparation by a nurse before transfer to the surgical suite. Physical patient care cannot be performed by an RPA robot through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Send patient to surgical suite
assessedActivities.reason: Moving the patient to the explicitly named destination is a straightforward transfer, supporting criterion 5. It is nevertheless a physical activity rather than an application-interface operation.

assessedActivities.name: Provide post-surgical care
assessedActivities.reason: The nurse provides direct clinical care after the patient's return from surgery. This physical care is outside RPA, and no qualifying execution rules or software interactions are specified.

assessedActivities.name: Transfer patient back to surgical ward
assessedActivities.reason: The specified return transfer does not itself require creative content or complex interpretation, supporting criterion 5. Moving a patient physically cannot be automated through software user interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Order lab test
assessedActivities.reason: The model does not specify the test, selection rules, ordering application, or digital inputs. It therefore cannot establish that ordering is a noninterpretive software operation suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Create surgery report
assessedActivities.reason: The surgeon creates a report that is subsequently printed, supporting an inference of human software use under criterion 1. However, no content-generation rules, template, or complete digital inputs establish that RPA can author the clinical report.

assessedActivities.name: Print surgery report
assessedActivities.reason: Printing the report immediately after its creation supports a human software operation on an existing digital document, satisfying criteria 1 and 8. Invoking printing requires no clinical interpretation under criterion 5 and can be performed by RPA through the application's interface.

assessedActivities.name: Choose book
assessedActivities.reason: The customer's choice has no modeled selection rules or software interaction. The model therefore does not establish a basis for RPA automation.

assessedActivities.name: Take book to lending desk
assessedActivities.reason: Taking a book to the lending desk is straightforward and does not require creativity or complex interpretation (criterion 5). It is physical work and cannot be performed by an RPA software robot.

assessedActivities.name: Request library card
assessedActivities.reason: Making a library-card request is a straightforward action (criterion 5), triggered by the library-card validity check. No digital request channel or application interaction is modeled, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Choose different book
assessedActivities.reason: The reservation check prompts another customer choice, but the model specifies neither selection rules nor a software interface for that choice. RPA automation is therefore not supported.

assessedActivities.name: Receive book
assessedActivities.reason: Receiving the book requires no creativity or complex interpretation (criterion 5). In the lending-desk context this is a physical handover, not an activity executable through application user interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Check availability of book
assessedActivities.reason: The subsequent 'Book reserved?' gateway supports a definite reservation-status check that requires no creative interpretation (criteria 2 and 5). However, no digital reservation records or software interaction are identified, so the model does not establish that RPA can perform the check.

assessedActivities.name: Explain additional conditions
assessedActivities.reason: The model does not specify the additional conditions, a standardized explanation, or a digital communication channel. Neither rule-based execution nor delivery through an application interface is established.

assessedActivities.name: Register borrowing
assessedActivities.reason: Recording the borrowing after the eligibility checks is a routine, noncreative action (criterion 5). The model does not identify an electronic register or any software interface, so it cannot establish RPA feasibility rather than potentially paper-based registration.

assessedActivities.name: Disassemble filling funnel
assessedActivities.reason: This is physical equipment disassembly, not interaction with software interfaces. The model does not establish any feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Empty? Product-free?

assessedActivities.name: Check funnel outlet
assessedActivities.reason: The context indicates inspection of a physical funnel outlet, without digital inputs or defined inspection rules. No feasibility criteria or basis for UI-based RPA are established.

assessedActivities.name: Remove sieves
assessedActivities.reason: Removing specified equipment components does not require creativity or complex interpretation (criterion 5). It nevertheless requires physical work rather than software-interface interaction.

assessedActivities.name: Check sieves and vibratory chutes
assessedActivities.reason: This is an equipment inspection following sieve removal. Neither digital inspection data nor explicit evaluation rules are provided, so no criteria or RPA feasibility are established.

assessedActivities.name: Remove plexiglass covers and outlet at vibratory chutes
assessedActivities.reason: Removal of identified covers and an outlet supports criterion 5 because no creative or interpretive work is indicated. The physical removal itself cannot be performed through RPA software interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Check clearance spaces beneath vibratory chutes
