assessedActivities.name: Inform student
assessedActivities.reason: The Office of Academic Affairs uses CMS to notify the student of a degree already generated there, supporting criteria 1 and 8. Communicating the specified notification and instructions does not require complex interpretation (criterion 5) and can be performed through the CMS interface.

assessedActivities.name: Check information
assessedActivities.reason: The student checks information before deciding whether to change assignments or include additional subjects. No validation rules or other evidence establish that this review can be performed by RPA without student judgment.

assessedActivities.name: Re-send information
assessedActivities.reason: The office re-sends existing digital information through CMS, supporting criteria 1, 5 and 8. The timer and loop-limit gateway provide an explicit conditional retry rule (criterion 2), making this a suitable RPA notification step.

assessedActivities.name: Edit certificate-relevant information
assessedActivities.reason: The student edits assignments and subject selections in CMS, supporting human software use and structured data (criteria 1 and 7). However, the activity includes deciding which assignments to retain or change and which additional subjects to report, with no rules enabling RPA to make those choices.

assessedActivities.name: Create certificate, degree certificate, diploma supplement
assessedActivities.reason: The preceding CMS degree generation and certificate-information editing support interpreting this as document generation from degree records. Compiling certificates with specified fields such as grades, ECTS grade and study-abroad period supports criteria 5 and 7 and is suitable for RPA in this context.

assessedActivities.name: Sign certificate, degree certificate, diploma supplement
assessedActivities.reason: Signing is assigned to the PA Chair, and the subsequent collection or registered-mail delivery indicates a physical-document context. No digital signing application or delegated signing mechanism is specified, so RPA feasibility is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Sign certificate, degree certificate, diploma supplement
assessedActivities.reason: Signing is assigned to the Dean within a process ending in physical document collection or registered-mail delivery. The model provides no software-based signing mechanism that RPA could operate.

assessedActivities.name: Create certifications and cover letter, store a copy in Regisafe
assessedActivities.reason: The CMS and Regisafe annotations explicitly identify applications used by the Office of Academic Affairs (criterion 1). Preparing accompanying documents and storing a copy are routine document-processing operations in this context (criterion 5), suitable for RPA through those applications.

assessedActivities.name: Collect documents
assessedActivities.reason: Collection by the student is the alternative to registered-mail delivery, indicating physical pickup rather than software interaction. Although pickup does not require creativity or complex interpretation (criterion 5), RPA cannot perform the physical activity.

assessedActivities.name: Send documents by registered mail
assessedActivities.reason: Sending the completed documents by registered mail involves physical dispatch and cannot be completed through application interfaces alone. The routine dispatch activity supports criterion 5, but its physical nature excludes RPA automation of the whole activity.

This routing action does not itself require creative interpretation and has one modeled continuation to the revision end state (criteria 1, 5 and 9).

assessedActivities.name: Forward the report to another clerk
assessedActivities.reason: Within the software-supported clerk workflow, forwarding is a noncreative routing action with one modeled continuation back to review (criteria 1, 5 and 9). RPA can execute the forwarding action, although the model does not establish an automated rule for choosing the receiving clerk.

assessedActivities.name: Reject report
assessedActivities.reason: Following the outcome-selection gateway, this activity records rejection in the software-supported workflow and leads directly to the not-approved end state. Executing that selected outcome supports criteria 1, 5 and 9, without establishing that the substantive rejection decision is automatable.

activities.name: Review travel expense report
activities.reason: The clerk lane and the 'Display all processes' annotation support human interaction with software (criterion 1). No review rules are specified, so the model does not establish that the substantive review can be automated.

activities.name: Adjust billing data
activities.reason: The display and upload annotations indicate software use, and the listed billing fields support structured data (criteria 1 and 7). The model does not specify how corrected values are determined, so automation of the complete adjustment activity is not established.

activities.name: Enter comment
activities.reason: The display annotation supports software use, and the activity has a single modeled continuation (criteria 1 and 9). No predefined comment or source for its content is supplied, so automating the complete activity would require unsupported assumptions about comment composition.

activities.name: Approve report
activities.reason: In the software-supported clerk workflow, this activity executes the approval outcome after the branching gateway and leads directly to the approved end state. Recording that selected outcome is a noncreative software action with one modeled continuation (criteria 1, 5 and 9); automating the preceding approval decision is not implied.

activities.name: Return report to applicant
activities.reason: The software-supported workflow provides context for returning the report to its applicant after that outcome is selected. This routing action does not itself require creative interpretation and has one modeled continuation to the revision end state (criteria 1, 5 and 9).

RPA can execute the forwarding action, although the model does not establish an automated rule for choosing the receiving clerk.

assessedActivities.name: establish ID

assessedActivities.name: document Proces start

assessedActivities.name: save data

assessedActivities.name: remind support employee

assessedActivities.name: close ticket
assessedActivities.reason: The parallel join explicitly gates ticket closure on completion of the preceding branches (criterion 2). Closing the digital ticket is a routine structured-record operation with no alternative outcome modeled (criteria 5, 7, 8 and 9), supporting RPA.

assessedActivities.name: fill formular
assessedActivities.reason: The employee fills a form that feeds system data saving, supporting human software use, structured fields and one completion path (criteria 1, 7 and 9). assessedActivities.name: determine email

assessedActivities.name: determine customer nr.

assessedActivities.name: categorize problem

assessedActivities.name: change prioritization

assessedActivities.name: problem viewing

assessedActivities.name: check DB for known problem

assessedActivities.name: determine support employee
assessedActivities.reason: The activity has one modeled completion path (criterion 9). No assignment rules, staff data source or application is identified, so selecting a support employee cannot be established as RPA-feasible.

assessedActivities.name: capture working time
assessedActivities.reason: Recording working time involves simple, structured time values and has one completion path (criteria 5, 7 and 9). The model does not identify a time-recording application or digital time source, so UI-based automation remains unsupported.

assessedActivities.name: write summary
assessedActivities.reason: The summary activity has one modeled completion path (criterion 9). No template or composition rules demonstrate that writing it can be automated without interpreting the problem and its resolution.

assessedActivities.name: order mail
assessedActivities.reason: Between selecting a support employee and confirming the problem, this activity can be inferred as emailing the assignment using the digital problem information (criteria 1 and 8). assessedActivities.name: write e-mail

assessedActivities.name: call

assessedActivities.name: fill formular

login

assessedActivities.name: Listen to complaint

assessedActivities.name: Log financing application
assessedActivities.reason: Logging an application is routine recording rather than creative work (criterion 5). However, the model does not specify a software application or digital input, so UI-based automation cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Forward application to credit department
assessedActivities.reason: The destination is explicitly specified and forwarding requires no complex interpretation (criteria 2 and 5). The model does not establish whether the handoff is electronic or physical.

assessedActivities.name: Enter information
assessedActivities.reason: The credit department performs information entry using the explicitly associated Credit department system (criterion 1). This routine entry operation supports criterion 5 and is a candidate for RPA, although the input format and availability are unspecified.

assessedActivities.name: Check creditworthiness
assessedActivities.reason: The Credit department system annotation supports human use of software (criterion 1). However, no assessment rules or thresholds establish that the creditworthiness decision can be executed by RPA without judgment.

assessedActivities.name: Note results
assessedActivities.reason: Recording the results of the preceding check supports criterion 5. The model does not establish that the results are recorded electronically rather than on paper, so RPA feasibility remains uncertain.

assessedActivities.name: Forward application to business practices department
assessedActivities.reason: Forwarding to a specified department provides an unambiguous routing instruction and requires no complex interpretation (criteria 2 and 5). No electronic transfer mechanism is identified.

assessedActivities.name: Check customer requirements
assessedActivities.reason: This check determines whether the standard contract needs adjustment, but the model supplies neither decision rules nor a supporting application. It does not establish that the assessment can be automated without interpreting customer requirements.

assessedActivities.name: Adjust standard contract
assessedActivities.reason: The Business Practices system annotation supports human software use (criterion 1). However, the model gives no rules for translating customer requirements into contract adjustments, so automation of the substantive changes is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Attach special conditions
assessedActivities.reason: Attaching conditions after the contract adjustment is a routine assembly operation (criterion 5). The model does not identify the attachment medium or establish that this operation occurs in software.

assessedActivities.name: Forward application to pricing specialist
assessedActivities.reason: The named recipient makes routing unambiguous, and forwarding requires no creative interpretation (criteria 2 and 5). The model leaves the transfer medium unspecified, preventing a supported RPA classification.

assessedActivities.name: Enter information
assessedActivities.reason: Information entry by the pricing specialist is a routine operation (criterion 5). Unlike the credit department entry activity, this activity has no system annotation or other evidence establishing a software-based destination.

assessedActivities.name: Determine appropriate interest rate
assessedActivities.reason: The model provides no pricing formula, rate table, decision rules, or supporting application. Determining an appropriate rate therefore cannot be established as a rule-based RPA operation.

assessedActivities.name: Note interest rate
assessedActivities.reason: Recording an already determined numeric rate is noncreative and uses a structured value (criteria 5 and 7). The model does not specify an electronic recording destination or digital availability.

assessedActivities.name: Forward application to administrative group
assessedActivities.reason: The explicit destination supports unambiguous routing without complex interpretation (criteria 2 and 5). There is no evidence that the handoff uses an application rather than physical documents.

assessedActivities.name: Create offer letter
assessedActivities.reason: Although this activity follows determination of the financing terms, the model identifies no letter template, composition rules, or software application. It therefore does not establish that letter creation can be automated with RPA.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Enter delivery address and contact details

actualNamesWithIds.name: Add goods to shopping cart
actualNamesWithIds.reason: In this online-shopping context, adding goods to the cart is a customer software interaction that can be reproduced through the interface. The activity describes cart entry rather than product-selection judgment and has one modeled continuation.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Save order information
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Customer Service saves delivery data received from the online order into the Order information store, supporting straightforward software-based persistence of structured digital data. No alternative execution path is modeled.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Initialize payment
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Following order storage, Customer Service initiates the online payment exchange with the payment provider, supporting an RPA-executable software action rather than a judgment task. Payment success is handled downstream, not as an alternative within initialization.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Create picking list
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Following confirmation of an online order, compiling its goods into a picking list is a structured information-preparation activity suitable for RPA. actualNamesWithIds.name: Print shipping label with address

actualNamesWithIds.name: Mark order as delivered
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Receipt of delivery confirmation provides an unambiguous trigger to set the order's status to delivered in the Order information store. This is a straightforward Customer Service software update using structured digital order information, with no modeled alternatives.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send error message to customer
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The unsuccessful-payment branch determines when Customer Service sends the error notification in the online-order workflow. Sending that notification is a straightforward software action, although no message template or application stability is specified.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send order confirmation
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The successful-payment branch provides a clear trigger for Customer Service to send an online-order confirmation. The sending action requires no modeled complex interpretation and has a single continuation to warehouse processing.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send shipping order to logistics service provider
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The activity transmits shipping-order information from the online shop to the logistics provider after label printing, supporting an automatable information handoff rather than physical shipment. No complex interpretation or alternative sending paths are modeled, but the interface and data format are unspecified.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Process payment data
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The online payment exchange supplies payment information to the provider and produces payment information for status reporting, supporting digital, structured data processing. This context supports RPA feasibility, but the processing rules and application interactions are not specified.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send payment status
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The activity sends the processed payment result back to the online shop, where it drives the payment-success decision. Relaying this structured digital status is a straightforward information-transfer action with no modeled alternatives.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send delivery confirmation to online shop
actualNamesWithIds.reason: After package delivery, this activity sends a completion notification to the online shop, supporting an RPA-suitable information handoff without complex interpretation. activities.reason: The online-shopping context supports a customer submitting the cart and entered delivery data through software, using structured digital information without complex interpretation. Only one submission path is modeled.

activities.name: Enter delivery address and contact details
activities.reason: Entering address and contact fields in the online checkout is a straightforward human software interaction using structured data. RPA can perform the entry, but the model does not establish that the original source of every detail is digital.

activities.name: Add goods to shopping cart
activities.reason: In this online-shopping context, adding goods to the cart is a customer software interaction that can be reproduced through the interface. The activity describes cart entry rather than product-selection judgment and has one modeled continuation.

activities.name: View products
activities.reason: The online-shop context supports customer interaction with software, and no alternative paths are modeled. However, viewing products may involve personal evaluation, and the model supplies no objective or selection rules that establish an RPA-executable outcome.

activities.name: Save order information
activities.reason: Customer Service saves delivery data received from the online order into the Order information store, supporting straightforward software-based persistence of structured digital data. No alternative execution path is modeled.

activities.name: Initialize payment
activities.reason: Following order storage, Customer Service initiates the online payment exchange with the payment provider, supporting an RPA-executable software action rather than a judgment task. Payment success is handled downstream, not as an alternative within initialization.

activities.name: Create picking list
activities.reason: Following confirmation of an online order, compiling its goods into a picking list is a structured information-preparation activity suitable for RPA. The model supports a straightforward list-generation step, but does not specify its application or establish that every required warehouse input is digital.

activities.name: Pick and pack goods
activities.reason: Picking and packing goods in the Warehouse requires physical handling, which software-interface RPA cannot perform. The model shows only one execution path, supporting criterion 9 but not overcoming this physical limitation.

activities.name: Print shipping label with address
activities.reason: Printing an address label in the online-order workflow, with an associated Order information store, supports a software-driven printing action using structured address data. RPA can initiate printing; physical label attachment is not part of the named activity.

activities.name: Mark order as delivered
activities.reason: Receipt of delivery confirmation provides an unambiguous trigger to set the order's status to delivered in the Order information store. This is a straightforward Customer Service software update using structured digital order information, with no modeled alternatives.

activities.name: Send error message to customer
activities.reason: The unsuccessful-payment branch determines when Customer Service sends the error notification in the online-order workflow. Sending that notification is a straightforward software action, although no message template or application stability is specified.

activities.name: Send order confirmation
activities.reason: The successful-payment branch provides a clear trigger for Customer Service to send an online-order confirmation. The sending action requires no modeled complex interpretation and has a single continuation to warehouse processing.

activities.name: Send shipping order to logistics service provider
activities.reason: The activity transmits shipping-order information from the online shop to the logistics provider after label printing, supporting an automatable information handoff rather than physical shipment. No complex interpretation or alternative sending paths are modeled, but the interface and data format are unspecified.

activities.name: Process payment data
activities.reason: The online payment exchange supplies payment information to the provider and produces payment information for status reporting, supporting digital, structured data processing. This context supports RPA feasibility, but the processing rules and application interactions are not specified.

activities.name: Send payment status
activities.reason: The activity sends the processed payment result back to the online shop, where it drives the payment-success decision. Relaying this structured digital status is a straightforward information-transfer action with no modeled alternatives.

activities.name: Plan delivery date
activities.reason: Only one planning path is modeled, but no scheduling rules, software, or required planning data are identified. The context does not establish whether delivery-date planning can be performed through RPA without complex judgment.

activities.name: Deliver package
activities.reason: Delivering a package is physical logistics work and cannot be performed by a software robot through application interfaces. A single modeled execution path supports criterion 9 only.

activities.name: Send delivery confirmation to online shop
activities.reason: After package delivery, this activity sends a completion notification to the online shop, supporting an RPA-suitable information handoff without complex interpretation. The model does not establish how physical delivery completion becomes digital input or specify the sending application.

assessedActivities.name: Check whether the patient is ready for discharge
assessedActivities.reason: The model shows only two discharge-readiness outcomes, supporting criterion 9. It provides neither explicit clinical decision rules nor software-based inputs that would establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Conducting the dismissal interview
assessedActivities.reason: The interview has a single modeled continuation, supporting criterion 9, but involves interpersonal interaction rather than a specified application-based procedure. No scripted rules or software interactions establish that RPA can perform it.

assessedActivities.name: Explaining the documents and next steps
assessedActivities.reason: Only two subsequent paths are modeled, supporting criterion 9. The explanation is a caregiver communication activity with no specified script, digital delivery mechanism, or predictable software interaction.

assessedActivities.name: Dispense medication
assessedActivities.reason: Dispensing medication is physical work and cannot be performed by an RPA software robot. Its single modeled continuation supports criterion 9 but does not make the physical activity automatable.

assessedActivities.name: Issue the prescription
assessedActivities.reason: The activity has one modeled continuation, supporting criterion 9. The model does not specify electronic prescribing, available digital prescription data, or issuance rules, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Issue discard papers
assessedActivities.reason: The activity proceeds directly to completion without modeled alternatives, supporting criterion 9. Nothing establishes whether issuing the papers means physical handover or a software-based operation, so it cannot be classified as RPA-automatable.

assessedActivities.name: Checking the patient's status
assessedActivities.reason: A single continuation supports criterion 9. The doctor's status assessment has no specified decision rules, digital records, or application interactions from which RPA feasibility could be inferred.

assessedActivities.name: Check whether a final medical examination is necessary
assessedActivities.reason: The examination decision has only two modeled outcomes, supporting criterion 9. The model supplies no unambiguous medical criteria or software-based assessment procedure that would enable RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct the examination
assessedActivities.reason: Conducting a medical examination is a clinical patient-facing activity, not an operation that an RPA robot can perform through application interfaces. Its single modeled continuation supports criterion 9 only.

assessedActivities.name: Preparing the discharge report
assessedActivities.reason: The report preparation has no modeled exception or alternative execution path, supporting criterion 9. The associated discharge report does not establish structured or digital inputs, a template, or rules that remove clinical interpretation.

assessedActivities.name: Check whether Patient needs medication
assessedActivities.reason: Only two medication-need outcomes are modeled, supporting criterion 9. No explicit prescribing criteria or digital assessment mechanism establish that this clinical decision can be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Preparation of discharge documents
assessedActivities.reason: Document preparation has a single modeled continuation, supporting criterion 9. The administrative context and incoming report do not establish document templates, digital data availability, or an application-based preparation procedure.

assessedActivities.name: Planning the exit interview
assessedActivities.reason: The model specifies neither scheduling rules nor calendar software or digital availability data. Timeout and legal-deadline paths also return to planning, so a simple exception-free execution is not established.

assessedActivities.name: send invitation to supervisor
assessedActivities.reason: The supervisor-existence gateway gives a clear condition for this straightforward sending step, supporting criteria 2 and 5, and it has one continuation, supporting criterion 9. However, no electronic communication channel or application is specified, so RPA feasibility remains unestablished.

assessedActivities.name: Check whether medication is available
assessedActivities.reason: The stock-availability check is a straightforward binary determination with two modeled outcomes, supporting criteria 2, 5, and 9. No inventory application or digital stock records are identified, so the model does not establish that the check can be performed through software interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Present portfolio
assessedActivities.reason: Presenting suitable products, logistics and prices to the customer is not described as a standardized software operation. No presentation rules, digital inputs or predictable application interactions are established.

assessedActivities.name: Visit and advise customer
assessedActivities.reason: The activity involves a customer visit and expert advisory services, including walks, teardowns and design. Physical attendance and expert judgment cannot be replaced by RPA user-interface interactions.

assessedActivities.name: Create concept
assessedActivities.reason: Creating a concept following customer advice implies design or interpretation, with no deterministic creation rules supplied. The model identifies neither suitable application interactions nor structured inputs for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Write travel report

assessedActivities.name: Check payment
assessedActivities.reason: The day-30 check tests payment completeness and produces either success or continued nonreceipt. This binary account-payment status check in the bank's collection process supports inferring a routine RPA operation.

activities.name: Send invoice by email
activities.reason: The model specifies sending a digital invoice by email on the first day of the month, supporting a clear scheduling rule and routine digital transmission. This can be performed through an email application's interface, with no sending exceptions modeled.

activities.name: Suspend internet
activities.reason: Nonreceipt of payment explicitly triggers suspension, supporting a clear, noncreative action with few subsequent paths. However, the model does not establish whether suspension is a software operation or requires physical intervention, so UI-based RPA feasibility cannot be determined.

activities.name: Close account
activities.reason: Continued nonreceipt of payment after suspension provides an explicit trigger for closing the ISP account. The account-administration context supports inferring a routine account-status operation suitable for RPA, with no alternative execution paths shown.

activities.name: Send payment
activities.reason: Sending payment after a late fee is a routine action with two modeled outcomes, supporting criteria 5 and 9. The payment channel is unspecified, so the model does not establish that the customer can execute it through a software interface.

activities.name: Send payment
activities.reason: Sending payment following an incomplete-payment notification is a routine action with a single modeled continuation. Neither a digital payment channel nor a software interaction is specified, leaving RPA feasibility undetermined.

activities.name: Debit money
activities.reason: The bank initiates a routine debit on day 7 and distinguishes only transaction success and failure. This scheduled bank-account operation supports inferring RPA suitability, although human software use and the data format are not specified.

activities.name: Debit money
activities.reason: The bank retries the debit on day 9 after the earlier transaction failure, providing a clear timing and retry rule with two outcomes. The routine bank-account operation is suitable for inferred UI-based automation.

activities.name: Charge late fee
activities.reason: The model places the late-fee charge on day 10 following unsuccessful debit attempts, giving an explicit charging trigger and a single continuation. This routine bank-account charge is a plausible RPA operation, although the fee calculation and application details are not supplied.

activities.name: Receive payment

result.name: Fill in request form for further examinations

assessedActivities.name: Obtain consent for anesthesia
assessedActivities.reason: Obtaining patient consent is not modeled as a software-based activity. The 24-hour deadline alone does not establish unambiguous rules for obtaining consent or support automation through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct anamnesis and physical examination
assessedActivities.reason: This activity includes a physical examination by the anesthetist, which cannot be performed through software user interfaces. The model provides no evidence that the activity satisfies the feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Fill in request form for further examinations
assessedActivities.reason: The request form supports structured data use (criterion 7), with Kardex as input and an Order file as output. However, neither the form nor Kardex is identified as digital, and no application interaction is specified, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Classify patient in ASA
assessedActivities.reason: The anesthetist classifies the patient using examination results, but the model supplies neither explicit classification rules nor evidence of software use. Naming ASA does not establish that the classification requires no complex interpretation or can be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Cancel surgery
assessedActivities.reason: Cancellation is described abstractly, without an application, digital inputs, or specified cancellation procedure. The surrounding gateways do not provide sufficient evidence to establish any feasibility criterion or infer UI-based automation.

assessedActivities.name: Check pulmunary function
assessedActivities.reason: The nurse performs a clinical function check and produces Pulmunary functions data; this is not modeled as processing existing digital results. No software-based procedure or other supported feasibility criterion establishes RPA suitability.

assessedActivities.name: Perform ECG
assessedActivities.reason: Performing an ECG is a physical clinical procedure rather than an activity executable through application user interfaces. The admission-day timing and EKG output do not establish digital inputs, software interaction, or rules sufficient for RPA.

assessedActivities.reason: The model describes a patient presentation but does not specify software use or rule-based handling of results. The Results data object establishes neither structured nor digital data, so the context does not support RPA automation.

assessedActivities.name: Examine patient
assessedActivities.reason: Examining a patient is a clinical activity involving direct patient assessment rather than interaction with application interfaces. The model provides no evidence of a rule-defined software activity satisfying the feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Order surgery to be performed
assessedActivities.reason: The surgery order follows clinical examination, and no unambiguous ordering rules or software interactions are specified. The output to Kardex does not establish that the store is digital or that issuing the order is a routine application-based action suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.reason: Explain further procedure to patient describes physician–patient communication without a defined script or software interaction. Access to Kardex does not establish digital data availability or rule-based execution.

assessedActivities.name: Arrange further examinations
assessedActivities.reason: Arrange further examinations lists possible diagnostic examinations but specifies neither unambiguous arrangement rules nor an application through which arrangements are made. Reading and updating Kardex alone does not establish its digital format or sufficient evidence for RPA automation.

assessedActivities.name: Check whether invoice amount has been received
assessedActivities.reason: The receipt check has a clear binary outcome and only two modeled alternatives, supporting criteria 2, 5 and 9. However, no digital payment records or application access are identified, so UI-based RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Notify legal department
assessedActivities.reason: The notification is a straightforward handoff to a specified recipient with one modeled continuation, supporting criteria 5 and 9. The message flow does not establish an electronic communication channel or software interface for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Verification of the invoice amount
assessedActivities.reason: The model does not specify the verification rules or the conditions governing the three subsequent alternatives. It also identifies no digital source or application through which RPA could perform the verification.

assessedActivities.name: File police report
assessedActivities.reason: The activity has one modeled continuation, handing the case to the public prosecutor, supporting criterion 9. No report preparation rules, digital inputs or electronic filing interface are specified, so RPA feasibility is unestablished.

assessedActivities.name: Issue summary proceedings
assessedActivities.reason: The activity has a single modeled continuation without local exceptions, supporting criterion 9. The model provides neither rules for issuing proceedings nor a software interaction that would establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: SCHUFA check
assessedActivities.reason: The check has one modeled continuation to the parallel join, supporting criterion 9. Naming SCHUFA does not specify the access channel, required inputs or evaluation rules, leaving UI-based automation uncertain.

assessedActivities.name: Review of payment arrears
assessedActivities.reason: The review has one modeled continuation to the parallel join, supporting criterion 9. Neither the rules defining a positive review nor digital arrears records and software access are specified.

assessedActivities.name: Close the case
assessedActivities.reason: Case closure has one modeled continuation to informing After Sales, supporting criterion 9. The model does not explain the closure operations or identify an electronic case-management application, so RPA feasibility cannot be determined.

assessedActivities.name: Create customer letter regarding blocking
assessedActivities.reason: Letter creation has one modeled continuation to customer notification, supporting criterion 9. No template, composition rules, digital customer data or software application is specified, so automated letter generation cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Determination of further procedure
assessedActivities.reason: The activity has a single modeled continuation to process completion, supporting criterion 9. The customer's determination is otherwise unspecified, with no decision rules or software context supporting RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Create job posting
assessedActivities.reason: The model identifies internal and external job postings as outputs but provides no templates, creation rules, or software context. It therefore does not establish that composing the postings can be performed through RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Publish external job posting
assessedActivities.reason: Publishing an already-created posting does not inherently require creative composition, supporting criterion 5. However, the model specifies neither a digital publication channel nor an application, so UI-based automation cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Find applicant
assessedActivities.reason: The model provides no applicant source, software system, or unambiguous search and selection rules. The recruitment context alone does not establish an RPA-executable activity.

assessedActivities.name: Induct employee
assessedActivities.reason: Employee induction is assigned to the Department Head without defined digital steps or rule-based procedures. The model does not establish that this potentially interpersonal activity can be automated through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct interview
assessedActivities.reason: The interview leads to a decision about applicant suitability, but no scripted questions or objective evaluation rules are supplied. The model does not support replacing this interpersonal assessment with RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Complete hiring process

assessedActivities.name: Admit patient
assessedActivities.reason: Admit patient is assigned to the MTA, but no software interaction, admission rules, or digital inputs are specified. The context does not establish an RPA-executable activity.

assessedActivities.name: Schedule surgery
assessedActivities.reason: Schedule surgery follows the surgery decision, but the model supplies no scheduling rules, application, or availability data. Its feasibility as a rule-based software activity is therefore unsupported.

assessedActivities.name: Perform medical checkup
assessedActivities.reason: Perform medical checkup denotes a physician's clinical examination rather than an activity performed through application interfaces. No criteria supporting RPA feasibility are established.

assessedActivities.name: Discuss anesthesia
assessedActivities.reason: Discuss anesthesia is a clinical discussion assigned to the physician, with no prescribed script or software-based interaction. The model does not establish unambiguous rules or freedom from complex interpretation.

assessedActivities.name: Discuss risks
assessedActivities.reason: Discuss risks denotes clinical communication rather than a specified software operation. No rules or standardized content establish that this discussion can be executed without complex interpretation.

assessedActivities.name: Decide on surgery
assessedActivities.reason: Decide on surgery is a physician's clinical decision following the checkup and discussions. The subsequent gateway identifies alternatives but supplies no decision rules that would support RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Write discharge letter
assessedActivities.reason: Write discharge letter in the outpatient department has no specified template, digital sources, or composition rules. The model does not establish that clinical letter writing avoids complex interpretation or can be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Check patient record
assessedActivities.reason: Check patient record specifies neither the record's format nor the checks to perform. A physician's review cannot be classified as rule-based digital validation on this evidence.

assessedActivities.name: Discharge patient
assessedActivities.reason: Discharge patient follows post-surgical care and is assigned to the physician, but no discharge rules or application operations are described. The context does not establish an automatable software task.

assessedActivities.name: Write discharge letter
assessedActivities.reason: Write discharge letter in the surgical ward follows receipt of a surgery report, but that report is printed before being sent. Neither fully digital inputs nor rule-based letter composition is established.

assessedActivities.name: Admit patient
assessedActivities.reason: Admit patient in the surgical ward is a nurse's activity preceding patient preparation. No software system, structured admission data, or execution rules establish its RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Prepare patient for surgery
assessedActivities.reason: Prepare patient for surgery denotes direct patient preparation by a nurse rather than application-interface work. The model provides no evidence supporting the feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Send patient to surgical suite
assessedActivities.reason: Send patient to surgical suite specifies a straightforward transfer to a named destination, supporting criterion 5. It involves physical patient movement, which a software robot cannot perform.

assessedActivities.name: Provide post-surgical care
assessedActivities.reason: Provide post-surgical care is direct nursing care after the patient's return from the surgical suite. Physical care is outside RPA, and no rule-based digital component is specified.

assessedActivities.name: Transfer patient back to surgical ward
assessedActivities.reason: Transfer patient back to surgical ward specifies a straightforward movement to a named destination, supporting criterion 5. The physical transfer cannot be performed through software user interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Order lab test
assessedActivities.reason: Order lab test specifies neither which test to order nor an electronic ordering system or selection rules. The model does not distinguish clinical test selection from routine order entry sufficiently to establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.reason: Create surgery report followed by Print surgery report supports an inference that the surgeon prepares the report using software, satisfying criterion 1. However, no template, composition rules, or source data establish that RPA can generate the clinical content.

assessedActivities.name: Choose book
assessedActivities.reason: The model provides no selection rules or software interaction for the customer's choice. The context does not establish that this activity can be performed through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Take book to lending desk
assessedActivities.reason: Transporting the book does not require creativity or complex interpretation (criterion 5), but it is physical work and cannot be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Request library card
assessedActivities.reason: Making a library-card request is a straightforward action supporting criterion 5. However, the model specifies no digital request channel or application interaction, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Choose different book
assessedActivities.reason: The reservation gateway motivates another customer choice but supplies no rules for selecting a replacement. Neither rule-based selection nor a software interface is established.

assessedActivities.name: Receive book
assessedActivities.reason: Receiving the book is a simple action without creative or complex interpretation requirements (criterion 5). In this lending-desk context it is a physical handover, not an activity executable by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Check availability of book
assessedActivities.reason: The following reservation-status gateway supports interpreting this as a straightforward status check (criterion 5). However, the model identifies no digital availability records or software application, so it does not establish that RPA can execute the check.

assessedActivities.name: Explain additional conditions
assessedActivities.reason: The model specifies neither the conditions nor a standardized explanation or digital communication channel. It therefore establishes neither interpretation-free execution nor an application-based method suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Register borrowing
assessedActivities.reason: Recording the borrowing after the preceding checks supports criterion 5 as a routine recording action. However, no application, digital register, or data format is specified, leaving software-based execution and RPA feasibility unestablished.

assessedActivities.name: Automatically detect malfunction
assessedActivities.reason: Detection is performed automatically by the machine, not through a modeled human interaction with an application. The subsequent control-panel display does not establish that detection itself can be performed by RPA or establish any feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Manually detect malfunction
assessedActivities.reason: The operator manually detects a machine malfunction, with no software interaction or explicit detection rules specified. The model does not establish any feasibility criteria or a basis for UI-based automation.

assessedActivities.name: Place support call
assessedActivities.reason: The operator contacts external support, but no software channel, scripted conversation, or structured information is specified. The subsequent decision about technician deployment does not establish that the call is a rule-based activity suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Resolve the fault using the assistant
assessedActivities.reason: The model establishes assistant availability but does not specify whether the assistant is software or what fault-resolution actions are required. Neither deterministic rules nor software-only execution are established, and another attempt may be necessary.

assessedActivities.name: Resolve the fault with help
assessedActivities.reason: Available help texts provide guidance, but their content, format, and required repair actions are unspecified. They do not establish unambiguous rules, digital inputs, or fault resolution through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Resolve the fault using a knowledge base article
assessedActivities.reason: An available knowledge base article does not establish that the actual repair is software-based or requires no complex interpretation. The model provides neither the article's instructions nor evidence that all necessary fault-resolution data are digital.

assessedActivities.name: Request technician
assessedActivities.reason: This is a straightforward request following the technician-availability check, with one modeled continuation to problem identification, supporting criteria 5 and 9. However, no application or digital request channel is specified, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Identify problem
assessedActivities.reason: Technician diagnosis is described without diagnostic rules, digital inputs, or software interactions. The model therefore does not establish any feasibility criteria or show that diagnosis can be automated through a user interface.

assessedActivities.name: Request service engineer
assessedActivities.reason: The operator makes a straightforward external request after the deployment decision, with one modeled continuation, supporting criteria 5 and 9. The message flow does not specify an application or digital communication channel through which RPA could make the request.

assessedActivities.name: Place support call
assessedActivities.reason: The technician contacts external support after an unresolved problem, but no scripted interaction, software channel, or structured inputs are specified. The model does not establish criteria supporting automation of this support conversation.

assessedActivities.name: Request service engineer
assessedActivities.reason: This straightforward external request has one modeled continuation to service-engineer resolution, supporting criteria 5 and 9. No software interface or digital request mechanism is identified, so the model does not establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Service engineer resolves the problem
assessedActivities.reason: The activity describes specialist resolution of a machine problem without specifying the repair actions or rules. There is no evidence that the work can be performed through software interfaces rather than requiring physical intervention or expert interpretation.

assessedActivities.name: Resolve the fault with support assistance
assessedActivities.reason: The technician receives external support assistance, but the instructions and repair actions are unspecified. The incoming message does not establish structured digital inputs, unambiguous rules, or software-only fault resolution.

assessedActivities.name: Completion and documentation in the machine logbook
assessedActivities.reason: The model shows a single final documentation step leading directly to completion, without an exception or alternative path, supporting criterion 9. However, it does not specify whether the logbook is digital or whether its entries can be generated without interpretation, so RPA feasibility remains unestablished.

assessedActivities.name: Resolve the fault with support assistance
assessedActivities.reason: The operator receives assistance from external support, but neither the repair procedure nor its execution medium is defined. A support message alone does not establish deterministic rules, fully digital inputs, or execution through an application interface.

activities.name: Set up machine
activities.reason: The format-change annotation places this activity in equipment setup, with no indication of an exclusively software-based configuration step. Neither UI-based execution nor any feasibility criterion is established.

activities.name: Test run
activities.reason: The activity concerns running the machine after setup rather than a specified application workflow. Test procedures, decision rules, and digital data are not supplied, so RPA feasibility is not established.

activities.name: Release / validate machine
activities.reason: The annotation identifies production-equipment validation tests and a document, but does not establish unambiguous acceptance rules or a digital document format. The model does not show that validation and release can be performed through software interfaces.

activities.name: Finish production
activities.reason: The activity is an abstract production-completion step followed by machine cleaning. No software actions, execution rules, or digital inputs support assigning criteria or classifying it as RPA-automatable.

activities.name: Clean machine
activities.reason: Machine cleaning is physical work and cannot be performed by a software robot through application interfaces. The annotation explicitly notes limited, customer-specific information, providing no further support for the criteria.

activities.name: Finish batch
activities.reason: The model does not specify whether batch completion involves physical operations, documentation, or software updates. No feasibility criterion or UI-based automation mechanism is established.

activities.name: Move produced products to the warehouse
activities.reason: The stated movement of products is a straightforward transport activity with no indicated creative or interpretive requirement, supporting criterion 5. It nevertheless requires physical handling and is not automatable with UI-based RPA.

activities.name: Move produced products to the warehouse
activities.reason: The stated movement of products is a straightforward transport activity with no indicated creative or interpretive requirement, supporting criterion 5. Physical transport cannot be performed by an RPA software robot.

Enter dates into ward board and Kardex

result.name: Arrange and coordinate appointments for examinations
Enter dates into ward board and Kardex

assessedActivities.name: Arrange and coordinate appointments for examinations
assessedActivities.reason: The model lists examinations and identifies Kardex as an input, but provides neither scheduling rules nor evidence of software-based coordination. The context therefore does not establish feasibility for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Enter dates into ward board and Kardex
assessedActivities.reason: Recording already arranged dates is straightforward transcription using structured date values, supporting criteria 5 and 7. However, neither the ward board nor Kardex is identified as digital, so interaction through software interfaces cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Order current medications and therapies
assessedActivities.reason: The activity is assigned to the ward doctor and records output in Kardex, but the model does not establish rule-based ordering without clinical interpretation. It also does not identify a software interface or digital inputs that would support RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Fill in request form
assessedActivities.reason: A request form provides evidence of structured data, supporting criterion 7. Its contents, completion rules, and digital availability are unspecified, so the model does not establish that this activity can be performed through software interfaces.

result.name: Update Kardex with planned lab examination

assessedActivities.name: Update Kardex with planned lab examination
assessedActivities.reason: Recording an already planned examination supports criterion 5, and the model shows no exception paths for this activity (9). The Kardex is not identified as electronic, so interaction with a software application cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Receive blood analysis results
assessedActivities.reason: Receiving results, rather than interpreting them, supports criterion 5, with no alternative paths modeled (9). Neither the transmission medium nor a receiving application is specified, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Label tubule
assessedActivities.reason: Labeling a tubule from the Kardex is a routine activity without modeled alternatives, supporting criteria 5 and 9. It involves labeling a physical object and cannot be performed solely through application user interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Fill in lab form
assessedActivities.reason: Transferring Kardex information into a lab form supports routine processing of structured fields (5, 7), with no modeled exception paths (9). The model does not establish that either the Kardex or the form is digital or accessible through an application.

assessedActivities.name: Take blood sample
assessedActivities.reason: The mandatory 10am deadline and emergency-lab routing if it is missed provide an explicit, compulsory rule (2, 4). Taking blood is physical clinical work, not an activity a software robot can execute.

assessedActivities.name: Prepare blood examination
assessedActivities.reason: The model gives preparation a single continuation without exception paths (9). It does not describe the preparation steps or any software interaction, so this abstract laboratory activity cannot be established as RPA-automatable.

assessedActivities.name: Examine blood sample
assessedActivities.reason: The activity examines a physical sample using examination machines, rather than describing application-interface work. Machine problems, lost samples, and defective samples are explicitly documented exceptions, and no feasibility criterion is sufficiently established.

assessedActivities.name: Lab physician validates results
assessedActivities.reason: The activity has no modeled alternative paths (9), but physician validation is not accompanied by explicit validation rules. The model establishes neither the absence of complex clinical interpretation nor a software interface suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Send results to ward
assessedActivities.reason: Sending already validated results is routine (5), uses the structured lab form (7), and has no modeled exception paths (9). The message flow does not specify electronic delivery or an application, so software-based automation cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Transport blood sample to Lab
assessedActivities.reason: The mandatory 11am arrival requirement is explicit and compulsory (2, 4), and transporting the sample requires no modeled complex interpretation or alternative paths (5, 9). Physical transportation cannot be performed by an RPA software robot.

assessedActivities.name: Update Kardex with planned examination
assessedActivities.reason: Recording an already planned examination supports criterion 5. However, the model does not establish that Kardex is an electronic application rather than a physical record, so UI-based RPA feasibility cannot be determined.

assessedActivities.name: Fill in form for consultative examination
assessedActivities.reason: The associated requisition form supports structured data under criterion 7. Neither an electronic form nor digital inputs or a software application are established, so RPA feasibility cannot be determined.

assessedActivities.name: Arrange appointment for consultative evaluation
assessedActivities.reason: The model specifies neither scheduling rules nor a scheduling application or digital availability data. Arranging the appointment therefore lacks sufficient evidence for any criterion or UI-based RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Enlighten patient
assessedActivities.reason: This activity concerns the ward doctor's communication with the patient, with no prescribed content or software interaction modeled. The model provides no evidence of a rule-based digital activity suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Obtain consent from patient
assessedActivities.reason: The declaration of consent documents the outcome but does not establish structured digital inputs, an electronic consent application, or unambiguous execution rules. Obtaining patient consent is therefore not established as automatable through software interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Check results
assessedActivities.reason: The ward doctor checks results before deciding treatment, but no mechanical validation rules are provided to distinguish this from clinical interpretation. The Kardex association also does not establish digital data or software use.

assessedActivities.name: Decide on further procedure of treatment
assessedActivities.reason: This is a clinical treatment decision, and the model supplies no unambiguous decision rules supporting criteria 2 or 5. Access to Kardex alone does not establish a digital, UI-based activity suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Perform consultative evaluation
assessedActivities.reason: The Council performs a clinical evaluation without modeled evaluation rules, structured inputs, or application interactions. No criterion or basis for replacing that evaluation with UI-based RPA is established.

assessedActivities.name: Draw up results
assessedActivities.reason: Preparing results follows the Council's clinical evaluation, but the model does not specify a template, transcription-only operation, or software application. It therefore does not establish either freedom from complex interpretation or a digital execution context suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Perform ultrasound scan
assessedActivities.reason: The model shows only a perform-or-skip alternative for this activity, supporting criterion 9. Performing an ultrasound scan is a physical clinical procedure, not an activity that RPA can execute through application user interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Perform cyst proktoskopy
assessedActivities.reason: The modeled perform-or-skip alternative supports criterion 9. Perform cyst proktoskopy denotes a physical clinical examination rather than software-based work that an RPA robot can perform.

assessedActivities.name: Perform pyeography
assessedActivities.reason: The model provides only a perform-or-skip alternative, supporting criterion 9. Perform pyeography is a clinical imaging procedure, and the model does not describe a separable application-interface task that RPA could execute.

assessedActivities.name: Perform CT/NMR of abdomen
assessedActivities.reason: The modeled perform-or-skip branch supports criterion 9. Performing CT/NMR of the abdomen requires a physical clinical imaging procedure and cannot be accomplished solely through RPA interactions with software interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Perform colon contrast image
assessedActivities.reason: The model shows a limited perform-or-skip alternative, supporting criterion 9. Perform colon contrast image denotes a physical diagnostic procedure, not a purely digital activity suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Perform gastrointestinal tract
assessedActivities.reason: The preceding timer enforces an unambiguous minimum six-day wait after Perform colon contrast image, supporting criteria 2 and 4 for the timing constraint; the perform-or-skip branch supports criterion 9. The colonoscopy gateway and clinical context identify a physical examination rather than work executable by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct drug treatment
assessedActivities.reason: Conduct drug treatment is clinical care performed by a nurse, not a modeled software interaction. No feasibility criteria are sufficiently supported, and RPA cannot perform the physical treatment.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct mobilisation, physiotherapy
assessedActivities.reason: Conduct mobilisation, physiotherapy requires physical patient care rather than interaction with application interfaces. The model provides no sufficient evidence for any feasibility criterion.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct weekly round
assessedActivities.reason: Conduct weekly round is a clinical activity by the head physician; its weekday scheduling rule does not establish rule-based execution of the round itself. The Kardex association does not establish digital data or software use, so no feasibility criteria are sufficiently supported.

assessedActivities.name: Conduct daily round
assessedActivities.reason: Conduct daily round involves clinical work by the ward doctor rather than a specified software task. Reading and updating Kardex does not establish that the record is digital or that the clinical activity satisfies any feasibility criterion.

assessedActivities.name: Treat the wound
assessedActivities.reason: Treat the wound is physical treatment performed by a ward doctor or nurse and cannot be executed through software interfaces. No feasibility criteria are sufficiently supported by the model.

assessedActivities.name: Remove drainages and threads
assessedActivities.reason: Remove drainages and threads requires physical intervention by a ward doctor or nurse, which is outside RPA capabilities. The model supplies no sufficient evidence for any feasibility criterion.

assessedActivities.name: Select a Pizza
assessedActivities.reason: The model shows a single continuation without exceptions (criterion 9), but provides no selection rules or software interface through which RPA could make the customer's choice.

assessedActivities.name: Order a Pizza
assessedActivities.reason: Communicating an already selected pizza order does not indicate creativity or complex interpretation (criterion 5). However, the message flow does not establish a digital ordering channel or application interface for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Ask for the Pizza
assessedActivities.reason: The 60-second event provides an explicit trigger for a straightforward status inquiry (criteria 2 and 5). No software-based communication channel is specified, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Pay the Pizza
assessedActivities.reason: Payment is a straightforward exchange with a single modeled continuation (criteria 5 and 9). The model does not specify a digital payment method or an application that RPA could operate.

assessedActivities.name: Eat the Pizza
assessedActivities.reason: Eating requires no creativity or complex interpretation and has no modeled alternative paths (criteria 5 and 9). It is a physical activity and cannot be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Calm Customer
assessedActivities.reason: The model provides one response path returning to waiting for another inquiry (criterion 9). It specifies neither an unambiguous response script nor a software channel, so this interpersonal activity is not demonstrably suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Bake the Pizza
assessedActivities.reason: The model shows a single continuation to delivery without exceptions (criterion 9). Baking in the Pizza Chef lane is physical work, not an activity performed through application interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Deliver the Pizza
assessedActivities.reason: Delivery has a single modeled continuation to receiving payment (criterion 9). Transporting the pizza in the Delivery Boy lane is physical work and cannot be performed by RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Receive Payment
assessedActivities.reason: Receiving payment is a straightforward exchange followed by process completion, with no modeled exceptions (criteria 5 and 9). No digital payment system or software interaction is specified for the delivery worker.

assessedActivities.reason: Organize ambulance service uses Kardex and produces a departure time, but the model does not establish digital access, software interaction, or explicit scheduling rules. Its abstract coordination context is insufficient to establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Prepare patient for examination
assessedActivities.reason: Prepare patient for examination is physical patient-care work performed by a nurse, not an activity executable through application user interfaces. Its association with Kardex does not establish any of the feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: Start of order
assessedActivities.reason: Start of order does not specify software interaction, digital inputs, or execution rules. Its machine-operator context does not establish that it can be performed through an application interface.

assessedActivities.name: Start of batch
assessedActivities.reason: Start of batch identifies a production stage but provides no evidence of software use or a defined digital procedure. The model does not support any feasibility criterion or establish RPA suitability.

assessedActivities.name: Setup
assessedActivities.reason: Setup occurs in a machine-operation context, but the model does not distinguish physical setup from software configuration. No rules, application interactions, or digital inputs are specified to support RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Release / validation
assessedActivities.reason: Release / validation has no specified validation rules, data sources, or software interface. Its position before production and logistics does not establish unambiguous decision-making or RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Production
assessedActivities.reason: Production in the Customer Machine Operator pool denotes manufacturing work rather than a specified application-based activity. The model provides no evidence of a UI-based procedure that RPA could execute.

assessedActivities.name: Logistics / warehouse
assessedActivities.reason: Logistics / warehouse does not specify whether the work involves physical material handling or digital administration. No supported feasibility criteria establish that this abstract activity can be automated through software interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Cleaning
assessedActivities.reason: Cleaning following production in the machine-operator context indicates physical work, which RPA cannot perform. The model supplies no execution details supporting the feasibility criteria.

assessedActivities.name: End of production
assessedActivities.reason: End of production identifies a closing stage without specifying software actions, data, or rules. The context does not establish an application-based activity suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: End of batch
assessedActivities.reason: End of batch does not describe a digital batch-closing procedure or any associated application interaction. Its sequence position alone does not support the feasibility criteria or establish RPA suitability.

    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0619tdw" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Event_199cfk1" targetRef="TextAnnotation_0ykio4b" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_06rc5y6">
      <bpmn:text>The “chip card” is the unique time tracking ID in ZEB. Assignment is also required even if no physical chip cards are used, for example when time tracking data is imported or when the QIS terminal is used.</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>

      <bpmn:text>QIS user role assignment (r_kollektionnutzer)</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0pui5wv">
      <bpmn:text>Time recorder, web time recorder and/or employee</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_1xdnwrs">
      <bpmn:text>Based on the working time data, ZEB determines the target working hours. In the case of multiple parallel employment relationships, a person’s target working time is the sum of the target working hours from the individual contracts.</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0abgn7s" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_192hz16" targetRef="TextAnnotation_1xdnwrs" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0hhrrc0">

    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0osmpmi">
      <bpmn:text>Reasons for deviating target working hours can include, for example, restrictions on part-time work for pregnant employees.</bpmn:text>

    <bpmn:association id="Association_0zdgajk" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_1bhzzu7" targetRef="TextAnnotation_0osmpmi" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_1b04o4k">

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send audio to cloud
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Send audio to cloud transfers an existing digital audio recording to the identified cloud recipient without interpreting its contents (criteria 5 and 8). This routine digital transfer is suitable for RPA, with one modeled execution path (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Play answer
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Play answer plays the digital response received from the cloud, rather than generating or interpreting it (criteria 5 and 8). Initiating playback is a routine operation suitable for RPA, and no alternative execution path is modeled (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Forward request to third-party skill
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Forward request to third-party skill transfers an existing digital request after the external-skill decision has already been made (criteria 5 and 8). This routine forwarding operation is suitable for RPA and has one modeled continuation (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send answer to device
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Send answer to device transfers the associated digital Answer to the local device without further interpretation (criteria 5 and 8). It is a routine transfer suitable for RPA with one modeled execution path (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Save interaction
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Save interaction stores the completed digital interaction in Usage protocols, without any modeled creative or interpretive work (criteria 5 and 8). This routine persistence operation is suitable for RPA and has one modeled path (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: Say command
assessedActivities.reason: Say command is a user's physical spoken action, not an application interaction that RPA can reproduce. It has one modeled execution path (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: Wait for answer
assessedActivities.reason: Wait for answer requires no creative interpretation and has one modeled path (criteria 5 and 9). However, it describes passive waiting by the user, with no software operation identified for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Record and process audio
assessedActivities.reason: Record and process audio combines capture of physical speech with unspecified audio processing; the model does not establish that these operations can be performed through application interfaces by RPA. Only a single execution path is modeled (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.reason: Process speech-to-text uses a digital audio recording and has one modeled path (criteria 8 and 9). Speech recognition requires an interpretation capability not established as an application operation that RPA can perform in this model.

assessedActivities.reason: Detect intent and determine context operates on the digital output of speech-to-text processing (criterion 8). Its semantic interpretation and subsequent external-skill decision have no specified rules, so the model does not establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Turn off machine
assessedActivities.reason: Turning off the production machine is a straightforward operation requiring no creativity, with no alternative execution paths modeled (criteria 5 and 9). It is an equipment operation with no software interface specified, so RPA feasibility is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Run machine empty
assessedActivities.reason: Running the machine empty is a straightforward equipment operation, followed by only two maintenance alternatives (criteria 5 and 9). The model does not establish a software interface through which RPA could perform this physical operation.

assessedActivities.name: Color detection: check calibration
assessedActivities.reason: The calibration check leads directly to completion without modeled exceptions (criterion 9). No calibration rules, digital measurements, or software interactions are specified, so the context does not establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Check pneumatic cylinders
assessedActivities.reason: The cylinder check has a single continuation and no modeled exceptions (criterion 9). It concerns physical equipment inspection, with no digital inspection data or application interface identified for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Check light barriers
assessedActivities.reason: The light-barrier check has a single continuation without modeled exceptions (criterion 9). Neither the maintenance-section annotation nor the activity specifies inspection rules or software interactions that would establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Check "slides" for visible defects
assessedActivities.reason: The visual defect check has no modeled exception paths (criterion 9). It requires inspection of physical slides, and the model provides neither digital images nor software-based inspection mechanisms, so it is not automatable with RPA as modeled.

assessedActivities.name: Perform initial examination
assessedActivities.reason: Perform initial examination involves examining the patient, rather than a specified software interaction. The Patient record does not establish digital inputs or rule-based execution, and the clinical examination cannot be performed by a UI-based robot.

assessedActivities.name: Take blood sample
assessedActivities.reason: Take blood sample is physical work on the patient and cannot be performed through application user interfaces. The model supplies no evidence establishing any feasibility criterion.

assessedActivities.name: X-ray patient

assessedActivities.name: Perform blood test

assessedActivities.name: Create blood test report

assessedActivities.name: Create X-ray report
assessedActivities.reason: Create X-ray report follows imaging and updates the Patient record, but no deterministic reporting rules or software interactions are shown. The model does not establish that reporting avoids clinical interpretation or uses entirely digital inputs.

assessedActivities.name: Perform final examination

assessedActivities.name: Write final report

assessedActivities.name: Issue prescription

assessedActivities.reason: The check has only two modeled outcomes, acceptance or revision, supporting criterion 9. The physician's assessment has no specified validation rules or software context that would support RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Sign medical report

assessedActivities.name: Send medical report

actualNamesWithIds.name: Note missing documents in the system
actualNamesWithIds.reason: The department records the missing documents in CMS after the completeness check, supporting criterion 1. Recording an already determined result is a noncreative software-entry operation suitable for RPA under criterion 5.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Automatically generate and send confirmation
actualNamesWithIds.reason: CMS automatically generates the confirmation using application information and the missing-document note already recorded in the system, supporting criteria 5 and 8.
