assessedActivities.name: Start of order
assessedActivities.reason: Start of order does not specify software interaction, digital inputs, or execution rules. The machine-operator context alone does not establish that this activity can be performed through application user interfaces.

assessedActivities.name: Start of batch
assessedActivities.reason: Start of batch identifies a production-stage activity without describing its execution or data. There is insufficient evidence for any feasibility criterion or for RPA automation.

assessedActivities.name: Setup
assessedActivities.reason: Setup occurs in a machine-operation context, but the model does not distinguish physical preparation from software configuration. No rules or application interactions are specified to support RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Release / validation
assessedActivities.reason: Release / validation has no documented validation rules, inputs, or software systems. Its position before production does not establish unambiguous decision rules or the absence of complex interpretation.

assessedActivities.name: Production
assessedActivities.reason: Production in the Customer Machine Operator pool denotes a manufacturing activity rather than a specified application-based task. The model provides no evidence of a UI-based activity suitable for RPA or of any feasibility criterion.

assessedActivities.name: Logistics / warehouse
assessedActivities.reason: Logistics / warehouse does not specify whether the work involves physical handling or digital administration. No software interactions, structured inputs, or execution rules are supplied, so RPA feasibility cannot be established.

assessedActivities.name: Cleaning
assessedActivities.reason: Cleaning following production in a machine-operation process indicates physical work, which RPA cannot perform through application user interfaces. The model does not document execution details supporting any feasibility criterion.

assessedActivities.name: End of production
assessedActivities.reason: End of production does not describe a software-based closure operation or its rules and data. Its placement after Cleaning is insufficient to establish any feasibility criterion or RPA suitability.

assessedActivities.name: End of batch
assessedActivities.reason: End of batch does not specify how the batch is closed or whether an application is used. The model supplies insufficient evidence of digital execution, defined rules, or other feasibility criteria to establish RPA suitability.

    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0619tdw" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Event_199cfk1" targetRef="TextAnnotation_0ykio4b" />
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_06rc5y6">
      <bpmn:text>The “chip card” is the unique time tracking ID in ZEB. Assignment is also required even if no physical chip cards are used, for example when time tracking data is imported or when the QIS terminal is used.</bpmn:text>

    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0pui5wv">
      <bpmn:text>Time recorder, web time recorder and/or employee</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_1xdnwrs">
      <bpmn:text>Based on the working time data, ZEB determines the target working hours. In the case of multiple parallel employment relationships, a person’s target working time is the sum of the target working hours from the individual contracts.</bpmn:text>
    </bpmn:textAnnotation>
    <bpmn:association id="Association_0abgn7s" associationDirection="None" sourceRef="Activity_192hz16" targetRef="TextAnnotation_1xdnwrs" />

    <bpmn:textAnnotation id="TextAnnotation_0osmpmi">
      <bpmn:text>Reasons for deviating target working hours can include, for example, restrictions on part-time work for pregnant employees.</bpmn:text>

activities.reason: The ERP annotation and Warehouse & Distribution lane support a staff-performed software availability check suitable for RPA. Checking whether materials are available is a straightforward, noncreative determination, and the model shows no exception paths.

activities.name: Obtain raw materials
activities.reason: Obtain raw materials supplies physical materials to Manufacturing product, rather than explicitly creating a digital procurement record. Although there are no modeled exceptions, supporting criterion 9, physical acquisition is not UI-based RPA work.

activities.name: Manufacturing product
activities.reason: Manufacturing product transforms raw materials into a physical product and therefore cannot be performed by UI-based RPA. Its single modeled continuation supports criterion 9, but no manufacturing rules or software interactions are specified.

activities.name: Ship product
activities.reason: Ship product concerns physical dispatch of the product, not an explicitly modeled shipping-system transaction, so it is not automatable with RPA. The activity has no modeled exception paths, supporting criterion 9.

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send audio to cloud
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Send audio to cloud transfers an existing digital audio recording to the identified cloud recipient without interpreting its contents (criteria 5 and 8). This routine digital transfer is suitable for RPA, with no modeled exception paths (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Play answer
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Play answer performs routine playback of the digital answer received from the cloud, rather than generating or interpreting it (criteria 5 and 8). Playback is a digital operation suitable for RPA, and only one execution path is modeled (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Forward request to third-party skill
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Forward request to third-party skill transfers an already processed digital request after the routing decision has been made (criteria 5 and 8). The forwarding operation is suitable for RPA and has a single modeled continuation to waiting for the response (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Send answer to device
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Send answer to device transfers the existing digital Answer to the local device without creating or interpreting its content (criteria 5 and 8). This routine transfer is suitable for RPA, with no modeled exception paths (criterion 9).

actualNamesWithIds.name: Save interaction
actualNamesWithIds.reason: Save interaction persists the digital cloud interaction in the Usage protocols data store, a routine storage operation not requiring creativity (criteria 5 and 8). It is suitable for RPA and has no modeled alternative paths (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: Say command
assessedActivities.reason: Say command is a user's spoken action, not an interaction a software robot performs through an application interface. It has one modeled continuation and no modeled exceptions (criterion 9), but is analog.

assessedActivities.name: Wait for answer
assessedActivities.reason: Wait for answer requires no creative processing and has no modeled alternative paths (criteria 5 and 9). However, it describes passive user waiting, with no application operation identified for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Record and process audio
assessedActivities.reason: Record and process audio receives a live voice command and produces an audio recording, with no modeled alternative paths (criterion 9). assessedActivities.reason: Process speech-to-text uses a digital audio recording and has no modeled alternative paths (criteria 8 and 9). assessedActivities.name: Turn off machine
assessedActivities.reason: Turning off the machine is a straightforward operation without complex interpretation, and no alternative execution paths are modeled (criteria 5 and 9). It is a physical production operation with no software interface specified, so RPA feasibility is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Run machine empty
assessedActivities.reason: Running the machine empty is a straightforward physical operation, followed by only two maintenance alternatives (criteria 5 and 9). The model provides no application interface through which an RPA robot could perform the operation.

assessedActivities.name: Color detection: check calibration
assessedActivities.reason: The calibration check proceeds directly to completion without modeled exceptions (criterion 9). Neither calibration rules nor digital measurements or software interactions are specified, so the model does not establish that RPA can perform this check.

assessedActivities.name: Check pneumatic cylinders
assessedActivities.reason: The cylinder check has a single continuation and no modeled exception paths (criterion 9). Its production-maintenance context indicates equipment inspection, with no evidence of a software-based check suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Check light barriers

assessedActivities.reason: This check has no modeled exception or alternative execution paths (criterion 9). It requires visual inspection of physical equipment, and the model provides no digital inspection data or application interaction that would enable RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Run test with printed folding box
assessedActivities.reason: Run test with printed folding box involves a physical test rather than a documented application-based operation. No test rules or digital execution mechanism are specified.

assessedActivities.name: Check reject entry in MSR
assessedActivities.reason: The subsequent gateway defines a straightforward entry-existence check with two outcomes, supporting criteria 2, 5 and 9. However, MSR is not defined as a digital application with an accessible user interface, so the model does not establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Check settings
assessedActivities.reason: Check settings occurs when the reject entry is absent, but the model specifies neither the settings nor the rules for checking them. It also does not establish whether checking involves software or physical equipment, leaving RPA feasibility unsupported.

assessedActivities.name: Admit patient
assessedActivities.reason: Admit patient has a single modeled continuation without exception paths (criterion 9). Although it produces a Patient record, the model does not establish software use or digital data, so UI-based RPA feasibility cannot be determined.

assessedActivities.name: Perform initial examination
assessedActivities.reason: Perform initial examination is a clinical examination of the patient rather than a software-only activity and is therefore not suitable for RPA. Its modeled continuation is a parallel split, not an exception or alternative execution path (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: Take blood sample
assessedActivities.reason: Take blood sample requires physical interaction with the patient and cannot be performed by UI-based RPA. It has one modeled continuation and no exception paths (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: X-ray patient
assessedActivities.reason: X-ray patient is a physical diagnostic procedure, not an activity executable solely through application interfaces. The model provides a simple ordered-or-not branch and a single continuation after the procedure, supporting few alternative paths (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: Perform blood test
assessedActivities.reason: Perform blood test follows collection of a physical blood sample and represents laboratory work, with no evidence of an exclusively software-based task. It has a single modeled continuation without exceptions (criterion 9), but the physical testing activity is not suitable for RPA.

assessedActivities.name: Create blood test report
assessedActivities.reason: Create blood test report has no modeled exceptions or alternative continuations (criterion 9). The model does not specify digital test results, reporting software, or deterministic report-generation rules, so RPA feasibility is not established.

assessedActivities.name: Create X-ray report
assessedActivities.reason: Create X-ray report has a single modeled continuation without exception paths (criterion 9). Its association with the Patient record does not establish digital inputs or rule-based reporting rather than clinical interpretation, so RPA feasibility is unsupported.

assessedActivities.name: Perform final examination
assessedActivities.reason: Perform final examination is a clinical examination and cannot be replaced by a robot interacting only with software interfaces. Its subsequent parallel split introduces concurrent work rather than alternative or exception paths (criterion 9).

assessedActivities.name: Write final report
assessedActivities.reason: Write final report has a single modeled continuation without exceptions (criterion 9). The Patient record and Final report have no specified digital format, and the model supplies neither reporting rules nor software interactions sufficient to establish RPA feasibility.

assessedActivities.name: Issue prescription
assessedActivities.reason: Issue prescription has no modeled alternative or exception paths (criterion 9). activities.name: capture order
activities.reason: The Sales department records ArticleID, Amount and Date in a Database, supporting human software use, structured data and routine data entry. This supports RPA, although the incoming order's format is not specified.

activities.name: forward order
activities.reason: Forwarding the order to Stock after database-backed capture is a routine information handoff without evident creative interpretation (criterion 5). The preceding digital capture supports inferring an RPA-capable handoff.

activities.name: make offer and sell
activities.reason: The activity follows advice to sell stock at a low price, but the model specifies neither pricing rules nor software-supported selling steps. It does not establish that offer creation and selling can be performed by RPA.

activities.name: send to customer
activities.reason: The Stock context and preceding commissioning indicate physical shipment of goods rather than digital transmission. Although shipment does not inherently require creativity (criterion 5), physical delivery cannot be performed by RPA.

activities.name: commision ware
activities.reason: Between stock availability and shipment, this activity represents routine physical picking or preparation of goods (criterion 5). Such warehouse work cannot be executed through application user interfaces.

activities.name: update inventory
activities.reason: The Stock department updates the Database using ArticleID and Amount, supporting human software use, routine record maintenance and structured data. This record-update activity is suitable for RPA, but the model does not establish that all inputs are digital.

activities.name: update inventory
activities.reason: This is routine inventory record maintenance following dispatch or receipt of goods (criterion 5). The connected database-backed inventory update supports inferring an RPA-capable record-maintenance context, although this occurrence has no explicit data associations.

activities.name: buy ware
activities.reason: The Purchasing department records ArticleID and Amount in the Database, supporting software use and structured data. However, the model does not specify supplier selection, purchasing rules or how the purchase is executed, so automation of the whole activity is not established.

activities.name: send in stock
activities.reason: Following buying goods and preceding commissioning, this activity indicates routine physical transfer into stock (criterion 5). RPA cannot perform that material movement.
